en: Om. Salutation to Viṣṇu.

Now, in the *khilas*, the purpose of the opening verses (*sūkta-pratīka*) and so forth has been stated, as well as the presiding deities (*adhidaivata*) and characteristics of the hymns beginning with the *śatarcins*. The sacrificial formulas (*yajūṃṣi*) consist of eighty syllables and so on, increasing by four each time—namely, *kṛti*, *prakṛti*, *ākṛti*, *vikṛti*, *saṃkṛti*, *abhikṛti*, and *utkṛti*. The enumeration of the number [of syllables] and so forth is the same; and for the seers (*ṛṣis*), when there is no specific instruction, the lineage (*gotra*) is the same. For the *khilas*, the number and other details should be understood as being exactly as those mentioned in the mantras that precede them.
//.(.Khila I Introduction...).

The triplet beginning with *śaśvat* consists of six verses; it belongs to Tārkṣya Suparṇa and the Aśvins. Among them, the seventh is addressed to Agni, the next (eighth) to Indra, the eleventh, ninth, and tenth have deities indicated by their internal marks (*liṅga-ukta-devatā*). The four verses beginning with the eighth are in the Virāj meter, while the [next] four are Jagatīs, including one Uro-bṛhatī. The seven verses beginning with *pra* belong to Brahmā; they are Niṣads and Upaniṣads. The second is a Jagatī, the sixth is a Virāj-sthāna. The ten verses beginning with *jyotiṣmantam* belong to Bhāradvāja Jyotiṣmān; the sixth and those beginning with the first have deities indicated by their internal marks, and are in the Anuṣṭubh meter, as are the ninth and the last two. The eleven verses beginning with *kṛśa* belong to the Aśvins; the first six have deities indicated by their internal marks, and are in the Anuṣṭubh meter. The seven verses beginning with *imāni* belong to Apunar-doṣa Indra.
The *āvaruṇa* is in the *jagatī* meter. This [hymn] consists of six verses by Retā Gaṅgya; when Yāmuni was the leader, he recited this triplet:
"May I behold the one of lofty majesty together with the most powerful Āditya.
I take upon myself the glory of the glorious ones and all forms. (RvKh 1.1.1)
Rising today, grant us our share, as a father does for his sons.
You are the master of long life; bestow that upon us, O Sūrya!
O Mitra-like one, great in glory, rising and ascending, O far-seeing one!
May we see for a hundred autumns; may we live for a hundred autumns.
Toward that ram, invoked by many, worthy of hymns...
O Nāsatyas, your greatness is ever celebrated; the cattle always praise you, O providers of abundant food.
When you two, O Aśvins, rescued Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, at his home on the path where there was no support;
when you, O Nāsatyas, striking down the white horse, brought Bhujyu with favor to Peru— those wise ones,
chanting that far-reaching delight in the assemblies, came to the thoughtful one, O wonder-workers.
O you who are praised by the wise, enjoy our libation; let your well-yoked swans carry you hither.
Come to us with your threefold chariot for the drinking of Soma, O celestial ones, to the libation for exhilaration.
The sacred grass is strewn for you both; the sweet libations are well-prepared. The Hotṛ-priests, chariot-borne and skillful-handed, are harnessed.
O Vāsātīs, wondrous ones, repositories of the moving world, O Heaven and Earth, O Rodasīs, hear me!
O Aśvins, lords of splendor, with donkey-steeds, come to my invocation together with Sūryā.

RvKh 1.2.6a: May there be portions of honey and ghee; let the powerful ones press out the potent Soma. RvKh 1.2.6b: In this very way, O youthful Aśvins, may your two arms milk forth nourishment with honey and ghee.
RvKh 1.2.7a: O Agni, may the moving hymns of praise delight you; they go forth toward that heaven and the Gharma-vessel.

May the fourteen-fold triple heaven, the youthful vigor, measure out wealth for us upon the well-established foundation. Impelling the golden stalk with care, O bountiful one, I urge on the bull to win the spoils.
Varuṇa, the one with bay horses and seven bay steeds, has yoked the rim of the three-naved wheel; may the Pragātha hymn bring him forth for our well-being.
Soma, Viṣṇu’s greatness, and power—the seven seers, the heroes, the men—delight them.
The sons of Sudhanvan, skillful-handed, with their labors [delight] Tvaṣṭṛ, Aṅgiras, and Ṛbhu for our well-being.
Here, here! (Here, here!)
O Maghavan, I place within your heart that firm and intense Bṛhaspati who is present there.

I bestow wealth upon the one who sits with the oblation; even the heated cauldron carries it for the sacrifice. Constantly do the two Suparṇas, the all-consuming guardians of the path who watch over men, [guard] the bird with loosened tail-feathers.

RvKh 1.2.13a: Ever and always, from the thirty-five [steps] that stand firm, ten more beyond;
RvKh 1.2.13b: he found the auspicious sacrifice, the thirty-nine-fold secret, with the sixty-eight as its sixth part.
RvKh 1.2.14a: He stood over the bull-like, well-heroic thunderbolt, the golden-hued, Indra-haired archer among the gods.

May the streams of honey and clarified butter flow forth, which you two, O wise ones, found within the cow. O Mitra and Varuṇa, makers of the world, may those Aśvins be pleased with my libations. [Bring] a comfortable chariot that travels a hundred paths, swift, moving at dawn, easy to mount, and golden.
RvKh 1.3.2b: Where the daughter of Vivasvat ascended, him indeed we bring hither for our protection.
RvKh 1.3.3a: Those horses of yours, chariot-borne, wise, swift as the wind, well-yoked and dripping with clarity;
RvKh 1.3.3b: with those by which you [came] to Sūryā as the bride, with those, O wonder-workers (dasrau), prosper us in battles.
O Aśvins, that generative seed of yours which is nourishing, by which the donkey [was born] from the barren woman, O bounteous givers;
from which he was born, longing for the gods and highly skillful—that, O physicians, you bestowed upon her, O celestial ones.
That medicine of yours, O Nāsatyas of wondrous luster, with which you aided Ghoṣā who longed for offspring.

RvKh 1.3.5b: May that which has been given to her by three men be bestowed upon the bride, so that she may obtain this skillful husband. RvKh 1.3.6a: O *dasras*, O *nāsatyas*, let the wise Hotṛ priest offer the *vaṣaṭ* call to you both at this pressed juice.
RvKh 1.3.6b: Let the noble woman, born of the *ṛta*, flow forth; let her joints relax for the sake of giving birth.

RvKh 1.3.7a: Thus you two, O sages, are both the manifest hymn and the secret doctrine; you are the two resounding ones, yoked together, the fair-winged birds. RvKh 1.4.1a: [I invoke] that chariot of yours, which is luminous, possessed of a banner, three-wheeled, easy to mount, comfortable, and full of wondrous power;
RvKh 1.4.1b: at the harnessing of which the one of wondrous wealth was born—him I call upon for you both, to drink the overflowing [Soma].
O Gods, joined with your ancient wisdom on your chariot, you who are worthy of sacrifice, come hither with your powers, O Nāsatyas; drink this third libation of Soma.
You two, the truthful ones, the thirty-three gods have placed you at the forefront of truth.
Rejoicing in our sacrifice and libation, O Aśvins, you whose fire is radiant, drink the Soma!
This deed of yours, O Aśvins, is worthy of praise: the bull [was sent] from heaven, from the mid-air, and from the earth. And those thousands who are eager for cattle—come to them all to drink!
RvKh 1.4.5a: This portion has been set out for you two, O worshipful ones; come to these songs, O Nāsatyas. RvKh 1.4.5b:
O Aśvins, drink the honeyed Soma; protect the donor with your powers. RvKh 1.4.6a:
[O you] who possess light, whose countenance is beautiful, who shine with undecaying luster like fires.
Make it auspicious for our offspring; do not harm man or the moving world.
May Dhātṛ, Rāti, Savitṛ, and Tvaṣṭṛ—since he became the messenger of Vivasvat—be pleased with this.
O Indra, being praised, together with the two Aśvins and Uṣas, grant us that vast domain of cattle.

RvKh 1,4.8b: Contemplating the powerful Soma, having brought him forth toward the vessel, he became the wellspring. RvKh 1,4.9a: Agni Pṛthu, Brahmaṇaspati, and Soma have come among the gods. RvKh 1,4.9b: O Indra, may [this] be under your sovereignty; O Bṛhaspati, these oblations are yours.
When the gods, generating the luster of the Brahman in the beginning, spoke [this], then the gods shall be under the control of that Brāhmaṇa who knows you thus.
O Lord of the World, you are emaciated; you, the wondrous one, protect the gods.
O Aśvins, Nāsatyas, who are well-disposed toward us, drink [the soma] that has passed the day.
O Suparṇa, bring him here; the sons of Heaven have established him.
Agni Jātavedas has become the lord of creatures, O far-seeing one.
Agni is the Hotṛ-priest, the all-pervading Vasu; he is the supreme glory of the gods.
May Agni be our protector, auspicious and a refuge, belonging to all the gods.
O Soma-drinker, protect us from every side as a source of wealth and bringer of fearlessness.
O Agni, strike down the vital organs of the enemies and [the weapons] of those who seek to harm us.
O Sūrya, you are the lord of long life;
grant that to us. O Mitra-like one, O far-seeing one, may we behold you rising and ascending for a hundred autumns; may we live for a hundred autumns. //8//

O Aśvins, with your wondrous deeds, you restored the sage Cyavāna—emaciated, blind, and aged—to youth; he who was without eyes and possessed a stout body became once more a young man, a husband for maidens. O powerful ones, whoever has invoked you with Soma, with oblation, with clarified butter, with sacred knowledge, or with his mind...
He bestows radiant treasure accompanied by Indra—treasure much-desired, winning in battle, and consisting of heroic sons.
O Heroes, let Saptavadhri now impel our prayer and our song toward you both.
Desiring the tree that rises from the ocean, the youthful one, make him not one who is devoid of strength.
The seven-fold bound one, well-handed, tied to the wooden beam, noble and peerless, the humped bull, called out.
You two shattered his tree, like the wielder of the thunderbolt acting as a mighty bull.
One [cow], emaciated yet desiring, was difficult to invoke; she was the one who brings the gift of the sun-like patron.

RvKh 1.6.1a: These portions of yours flow forth; O Indra and Varuṇa, [come] at the great pressing of the juices for you both. RvKh 1.6.1b: For at every sacrifice you hasten to the libations, when you bestow your favor upon the sacrificer who presses the juice. RvKh 1.6.2a: The obstructing plants and the waters have attained greatness through these two, Indra and Varuṇa.
RvKh 1.6.2b: Those two who stand at the far limit of the mid-air, whose path no godless enemy can assail;
RvKh 1.6.3a: Truly, O Indra and Varuṇa, the seven voices milk forth that wave of honey which drips with clarity.
RvKh 1.6.3b: With those [voices], O Lords of Splendor, protect the donor—he who, unassailable, guards the cow with his insights.
RvKh 1.6.4b: O Indra and Varuṇa, with those [powers] of yours that drip with clarity, bestow skill upon the sacrificer.
RvKh 1.6.5a: For the sake of great fortune, we have proclaimed the true majesty of Indra to you two, the radiant lords.
O Indra and Varuṇa, lords of splendor, protect us with the three times seven [rays] that drip with clarity.
O Indra and Varuṇa, when in the beginning you bestowed upon the seers inspired thought, the conception of speech, and sacred hearing, the wise ones,
performing the sacrifice, released those meters and beheld them through austerity.
O Indra and Varuṇa, bestow upon the sacrificers benevolence free from pride and an increase of wealth.
This Soma, well-prepared, rooted in the pressing-stones, adorned with hymns and recited with praises;
mixed with milk, exhilarating, and sung to by the Sāman—O you of beautiful jaws, it quickly flows around for you both.
Drink of this pressed juice, of his vigor, which has been purified through the woolly filter, O you who are most excellent.
Come hither with your bodies, showing yourselves forth; we desire the sweet draughts, for now our wisdom yearns for them.
Open wide the doors!
Gentle, trembling much, and seeking you both, this inspired thought calls out to you.
O Nāsatyas, mount your easy-to-ride chariot—rich in stalks, comfortable, and well-yoked.
Whether it be a hundred horses or seven gods that draw it, let those bay steeds, most swift to carry, convey you.

RvKh 1.7.5a: When you two came to the dwelling of Śāryāta Mānava with your glance, while being praised; RvKh 1.7.5b: Desiring the shared feast, Cyavana made the gods afraid—that very one is he [of you two].
RvKh 1.7.6a: O Aśvins, on your three-wheeled chariot, bring hither to us wealth consisting of brave sons.

When you two yoke the generous, swift, and much-desired steed, the hero who conquers in battle—O *dasras*, that chariot drawn by noble horses, bring it hither at our invocations; then let the rewards of our bodies come to us. These most praiseworthy sages move about like Turvaśas unbound in the midst of battles.

RvKh 1.8.3a: Hear our call; satisfy the desire of the one seeking the sacrifice; bring hither their oblations. RvKh 1.9.1a: O Bulls, go to him who drinks the pressed juice, who is accompanied by the gods, who has prepared the oblation, and to whom the offering is presented.
RvKh 1.9.1b: He prospers with food, a hundredfold, visible and worthy of praise; drinking the offered draught, he eats that which is delightful.
RvKh 1.9.2a: When the singer praises your invincible deeds, and when the singers praise those [deeds] at the soma-pressings;
RvKh 1.9.2b: May those [deeds] flourish here among the various peoples, you who consume the soma-drink at the sacrifice.
RvKh 1.9.3a: When you two eager bulls restored the head to Dadhyanc, O physicians, turn [your favor] hitherward.
RvKh 1.9.3b: Therefore, O youthful ones, being exhilarated, you both eat that which has been offered with the *vaṣaṭ* cry, [prepared] with thought and honey.
RvKh 1.9.4a: O Atharvan, do not say what I say; this honey of yours is inconceivable compared to other more heroic [beings].
RvKh 1.9.4b: When the Bounteous One (Maghavan) instructed Dadhyañc, he told you two [the Aśvins] that which was [hidden] by the horse's head.
When he came, firm and armed with the thunderbolt, Dadhyañc bestowed sweetness upon us for our two parents.
"Do not speak ill of me, O you of evil hearing"—when he said this, that was your glorious renown.
By those powers, O bulls, by which you [helped] Dadhyañc and Turva, the son of Kavasa, of Makha—
RvKh 1.10.1a: This Soma, wise and seeking the gods, goes to you both, touching the heart as he approaches the sacrificial vessel.
RvKh 1.10.1b: Most skillful in performing the oblations, whether with honey or with ghee, O Aśvins, this new hymn of praise goes forth to you.
RvKh 1.10.2a: The great [hymn], desiring the gods, gladdens you both, by which means you, unwearied, traverse all the pathways.
O Aśvins, you who enjoy many things, bestow through your excellent praise the all-nourishing cow that is beneficial to the seer.

That chariot of yours which possesses cattle, horses, and pleasant speech, which is full of light and desires to make desirable things desirable— O you two most eager for cattle, I, the charioteer, call upon that omniform chariot which I invoke.
RvKh 1.10.4a: Your chariot, O powerful ones, is well-rolling, easy to drive, much-desired, a finder of wealth, and a bestower of vital strength.
RvKh 1.11.1a: O gods, this is the ancient portion of the sacrificial gift, when you, the worshipful ones, were exhilarated by the libation.
RvKh 1.11.1b: This Gharma is purified by the *ṛc* verses; you two, the chariot-drivers, consume it as you speed along.
O you two bulls, when you restored the severed head of Makha, the physicians joined it back together;
therefore, men and sages ever praise that beautiful and wondrous body of yours when the soma is pressed.
With that [medicine] by which the gods struck down the wounds and with which they overcame the godless armies.
RvKh 1.11.3b: With that [head] by which those who held the Soma became immortal, bestow that upon the horse’s head.
RvKh 1.11.4a: Long ago, when they were shattered, the gods, through their sacrificial wisdom, did not leave behind the ships nor the firmament.
RvKh 1.11.5a: When your mother, the impetuous Saraṇyū, approached you, she covered the well-rolling chariot with her garment.
RvKh 1.11.5b: There, O lovers of sweetness, the ancient, well-guided, and bliss-bestowing draught of honey has been offered for you both with honey.
RvKh 1.11.6a: You two cause even the heavens to shine with the stars; you two placed the milks within the *śakvarī* verses.
RvKh 1.11.6b: You two created this great earth with plants; you two released the rivers to flow.
O lovers of sweetness, you two are sweet with your honeyed essences; you two are the healers, physicians with skillful hands.
You two are the charioteers on your chariots, O fierce ones, most auspicious, with [your powers] that drive away disease.
Grant me that sight for my eyes, so that I may see clearly and behold the sun and these quarters of space.
O Aśvins, bring hither the plump, self-sustaining, horse-drawn, and flowing waters that have the Dāsas as their masters.
Your gifts are like those of Aditi in heaven; your pure, bright milks have shone forth.
O wonder-workers (dasrā), when you [recovered] Rebha, who was hidden in the waters, seeking you and striving for strength from the abyss.
O Aśvins, you raised up the swift eunuch; the reciters of hymns magnify that vow of yours.
That [power] of yours which is in the two bodies, which is on the earth, which is in the plants, in the pressing-stones, and in the mid-air;
which is in the heroes, in the patrons, and even in the firmament—with those [powers], O youthful ones, grant us protection for a hundred years.
RvKh 1.12.4a: That which brings you wealth for the one who praises you, and by its power strikes down the threefold hostilities of the hater;
RvKh 1.12.5a: That three-wheeled, well-seated, well-yoked chariot of yours, with three seats, bannered, and swift as the wind;
RvKh 1.12.6a: You two carried a wife to Vimada; you two provided a cow that yielded her desire to Śayu.
O you two, deliver Atri from his bond with life; you released him from distress. O Aśvins, for the sake of the auspicious she-wolf who was calling out like rams, the father made the blind man a seer.
In that Ṛjrāśva, you placed two eyes; you revealed his world once again.

RvKh 1.12.8a: That eye of yours which is in heaven, that which is the fair-winged bird, by which you two, O immortals, behold all beings— RvKh 1.12.8b: grant that to me, O kinsmen of the gods, as you bestow the two eyes; may I find honor among those who desire much.
II. Adhyāya.
Khila, II Anukramaṇī.

*Oṃ*. One verse beginning with *mā* [is] *Bhadra*; five *Anuṣṭubh*s; one beginning with *jāgarṣi* belongs to Jātavedas; two [verses] on well-being (*svastyayana*); one beginning with *varṣantu*; one beginning with *hiraṇyavarṇām* is the goddess Śrī of the Bhṛgu lineage; [the hymn] beginning with *Śrī* destroys misfortune (*alakṣmī*); it is in the *Anuṣṭubh* meter, ending with a *Śakvarī*; [the verse] beginning with *hiṃsā* belongs to Agni; the fourth [verse] is a *Prastārapaṅkti*; the fifteenth consists of two *Triṣṭubh*s and an *Upariṣṭād-bṛhatī*; the following six verses concerning Śrī’s sons are addressed to the Viśvedevas; five verses beginning with *ciklītaḥ* concern Ānanda and Kardama; [the hymn] beginning with *mayi śleṣaḥ* is a *śleṣa* (concatenation) belonging to Jātavedas, starting with a *Bṛhatī*; [the section] beginning with *saṃsravantu* concerns the remnants (*saṃsrava*) and belongs to the Viśvedevas; the second [verse] and those following are in the *Triṣṭubh* meter.

The two *ṣṭubh* verses [beginning with] "ā te" are a praise for the sake of a progeny-bearing embryo; Prajāpati [is the deity]; the two [verses] for Indra and Vāyu; the fourth is a *bṛhatī*; the fifth is a *prastārapaṅkti*.

"Agni" [consists of] five [verses]; "jīvaputra" [is the deity]; the [verse] for Agni and Varuṇa is an *ati-jagatī*; it ends with an *anuṣṭubh* and a *triṣṭubh*. "Cakṣus" is a praise of the single Self. "Śaṃvatī" consists of six [verses]; it is a prayer for peace (*śānti*); it is in the *anuṣṭubh* meter; from the fifth [verse] onwards, they are *bṛhatī* and *jagatī*. "Swapna" is a single [verse]. "Yasyopa" is an *anuṣṭubh*; the [remaining] *vālakhilya* verses follow.
Do not fear; you shall not die. I protect you on all sides.
With my mace I strike the scorpion, and with my staff I strike the serpent that has approached.
With the speed of the sun’s chariot and with the strength of Viṣṇu’s arms.
By the flapping of Garuḍa’s wings, go to the earth, O you of great fame!
As soon as Garuḍa was born, the three worlds were shaken;
the entire earth, with its mountains, forests, and groves, was shaken.
The sky, with its moon and sun vanished, no longer shines with light;
the deities are terrified with fear, and the wind does not blow—Oṃ, obeisance!
O serpent, may it be well with you, O auspicious one; go far away, O highly renowned one!
RvKh 2.1.5b: Remember the words of Āstīka at the conclusion of Janamejaya’s sacrifice.
RvKh 2.1.6ab: Any serpent that does not turn back upon hearing the words of Āstīka shall have its head split into a hundred pieces, like the fruit of the *śiṃśapā* tree.
Agastya, Mādhava, and the great sage Mucukunda; the sage Kapila and Āstīka—these five are those who sleep in happiness. Homage to Narmadā in the morning; homage to Narmadā at night.

Homage be to you, O Narmadā; protect me from the crawling serpent. He who was born of Jaratkāru by the aged maiden, he of great renown—O serpent, may it be well with you; go far away, O one of great renown!
Speak auspiciously from the right; speak auspiciously from the left.
Speak auspiciously to us from the front; speak auspiciously from behind, O Kapiñjala.
Speak auspiciously with your sons; speak auspiciously within our homes.
Speak what is auspicious for us; speak what is auspicious and free from fear for us.
Speak what is auspicious for us below; speak what is auspicious for us above.
Speak what is auspicious, ever-auspicious for us; speak what is auspicious for us on every side.
Make our dwelling free from rivals in the east, auspicious in the south;
grant us constant fearlessness in the west and prosperity in the north.
You magnify youthful vigor like the drum of victors.
RvKh 2.2.5b: O you who have birds tucked under your armpits, speak to us with your hundred feathers!
RvKh 2.3.1a: You are awake in the world, O Jātavedas; you are awake wherever the sacrificer offers the oblation.
RvKh 2.3.1b: With faith, I offer this oblation; by that, you protect the secret name of the cows.
The auspicious Tārkṣya, with uninjured wheels, the great being, the crow among the deities;

the slayer of Asuras, the friend of Indra in battles—may we ascend him like a ship, he who is great glory. With outstretched hands, I seek refuge in this protection; may there be well-being for us in straits, and may fearlessness be ours.
May Śyāvāśva [sing] forth with boldness.
O radiant one, let the lightnings from the cloud in heaven rain down for you.
Let all seeds sprout; strike down those who hate sacred knowledge. Sing forth a deep and lofty hymn to the sovereign lord.
O Jātavedas, bring to me Lakṣmī— golden-hued, tawny, adorned with garlands of gold and silver, radiant, and made of gold. O Jātavedas, bring to me that Lakṣmī who never departs.
In whom I may find gold, cattle, horses, and men;
Whose vanguard is horses, whose center is chariots, and who delights in the trumpeting of elephants— I invoke that goddess Śrī; may the goddess Śrī be pleased with me.
I invoke here Śrī, who is made of bell-metal, adorned with gold, moist, blazing, satisfied, and satisfying; she who dwells in the lotus, is lotus-colored, and resides in the lotuses.
I invoke her who is moon-like, radiant, blazing with glory, the noble Śrī beloved by the gods in this world.

RvKh 2.6.5b: I take refuge in him whose rim is a lotus; may my misfortune perish; I choose you. RvKh 2.6.6a: O you who possess the color of the sun, born from austerity, the lord of the forest is your tree, namely the *bilva*.
RvKh 2.6.7a: May he, the friend of the gods, come to me, along with fame and the jewel.
I have appeared in this kingdom; may he grant me fame and prosperity.
I destroy hunger, thirst, impurities, and the greatest misfortune (alakṣmī). Drive away from my home all lack of fortune and lack of success.

I invoke here Śrī, who has fragrance as her door, who is unassailable, eternally nourishing, and bestowing abundance; she who is the sovereign of all beings. May we obtain the desire of the mind and the fulfillment of speech.
May the form of cattle, the excellence of food, and glory rest within me.
O Kardama, from whom all creatures were born, arise within me, O Kardama!
Clothe my family with Prosperity, the Mother who wears a garland of lotuses.
May the waters flow with unctuousness; may they be well-prepared for me in my home.
May you establish the goddess Śrī, the Mother, in my home.
[She is] like a full lotus-pond, prosperous, tawny-hued, and garlanded with lotuses.
O Jātavedas, bring to me the golden Lakṣmī, Sūryā.
Bring to me the golden Lakṣmī, Candra, who is moist, who possesses a lotus-pond, a staff, and a golden garland.
O Jātavedas, bring to me the golden Lakṣmī, Candra.
O Jātavedas, bring to me that prosperity which never departs,
in which I may find abundant gold, cattle, female slaves, and male servants.
He who entered into bliss ran toward Vibhāvasu.
Worship all glories; fashion for me a dwelling in my house.
With mud we cause the progenitor to attain manifestation.
He has bestowed and approached those desires which we have fashioned.
O Jātavedas, purify me and bestow upon me the increase of wealth.
May Agni release me from that sin and from all distress.
O Agni, great as Mitra, speak for us to the gods; speak for us for the favor of both heaven and earth.
RvKh 2.6.16ab: He who, having become pure and self-restrained, should offer clarified butter daily;
and he who desires prosperity should constantly recite this hymn of fifteen verses.
RvKh 2.6.17a: O lotus-faced one, O lotus-thighed one, O lotus-eyed one, O you who originate from the lotus!

O lotus-eyed one, grant me that portion by which I may obtain happiness. O giver of horses, giver of cows, giver of wealth, O possessor of great riches! May wealth be pleasing to me, O Goddess; grant me all my desires.
Sons, grandsons, wealth, grain, elephants, horses, cattle, and chariots—of these you are the mother for all creatures; may she grant me long life.
Agni is wealth, Vāyu is wealth, Sūrya is wealth, and Vasu is wealth.
Indra, Bṛhaspati, and Varuṇa release wealth as their prize.
O Vainateya, drink the Soma; let the slayer of Vṛtra drink the Soma.
May the possessor of Soma grant me the Soma of wealth, he who possesses the Soma.

Neither anger, nor envy, nor greed, nor an evil thought arises for those who have performed meritorious deeds and recite the Śrīsūkta. [I bow] to her whose abode is the lotus, whose hand holds a lotus, and who is resplendent with most brilliant white garlands and fragrant perfumes.
Bringing glory, splendor, long life, health, and auspiciousness, it is magnified;
it bestows grain, wealth, cattle, the gain of many sons, and a long life of a hundred years.
[I worship] the Goddess Earth, the consort of Viṣṇu, the daughter of Madhu, who is dear to Mādhava.
I bow to the goddess Lakṣmī, the dear friend and beloved of Acyuta.
We know Mahālakṣmī; we meditate upon the wife of Viṣṇu. May that Lakṣmī inspire us.
O lotus-faced one, O lotus-lake, O you whose eyes are like lotus petals, O beloved of the lotus, O you whose long eyes are like lotus leaves;
O beloved of the universe, O you who are favorable to the minds of all, place your lotus-feet within my heart.
Bliss is the mud, and the sacred tradition is spread out like a thick layer of clay.
May debt, disease, and the like, poverty, sin, hunger, and untimely death;
may fear, grief, and mental anguish perish from me forever.
[May I attain] the splendor of Lakṣmī, shining like the moon, and the sovereign glory of Śrī, shining like the sun.
We worship Mahālakṣmī, who possesses the luster and color of the moon, the sun, and fire.
O radiant one, let the lightnings from the clouds of heaven rain down for you;
let all seeds sprout, and strike down those who hate sacred knowledge.
O beloved of the lotus, O lotus-dweller, O you who hold a lotus in your hand, O you whose face is like a lotus!

O beloved of the universe, O you who are favorable to the mind of Viṣṇu, place your lotus-foot within me. She who sits upon a lotus-throne, with broad hips and deep [navel], whose eyes are as long as lotus petals— 2,6.26a: yā sā padmāsanasthā vipula-kaṭi-taṭī padma-patrāyata-akṣī gambhīrā/ 2,6.26b: [She who is seated on a lotus-throne, with broad hips and deep [navel], whose eyes are as long as lotus petals. 2,6.26c: [She who is] profound... 2,6.26d: ...[and] deep. Bowed by the weight of her breasts which are like the nave of a wheel, wearing a bright upper garment—
may Lakṣmī, who is bathed with golden jars by divine lordly elephants adorned with clusters of jewels,
and who eternally holds a lotus in her hand, dwell in my house endowed with all auspiciousness.
Siddhalakṣmī, Mokṣalakṣmī, Jayalakṣmī, Sarasvatī,
Śrī, Lakṣmī, and Varalakṣmī— may they all be gracious toward me at all times.
[I meditate on her] seated upon a lotus throne, bearing in her hands a boon-granting gesture, kusha grass, a noose, and a gesture of fearlessness, while pouring forth [nectar].

I worship that primordial Sovereign of the World, who possesses three eyes and a splendor equal to ten million rising suns. O Śivā, the auspiciousness of all auspicious things, the accomplisher of all goals! He of noble deeds, whose name is cherished day and night— RvKh 2.6.29b: I worship her, the primordial Sovereign of the World, who possesses three eyes and a splendor equal to ten million rising suns. RvKh 2.6.30a: O Śivā, the auspiciousness of all auspicious things, the accomplisher of all goals!
RvKh 2.7.1a: He of noble deeds, whose name is cherished day and night—

RvKh 2.7.1b: O Jātavedas, shine upon us for our fellowship and for life; may the divine people purify me. RvKh 2.7.2a: May they purify my thoughts and intentions; may all beings purify me. RvKh 2.7.2b:
O Jātavedas, whatever has been left unstated [may it be purified].
O All-Gods, purify me; O Jātavedas, purify me.
May our heroes be born together; may the firm [power] abide among the firm things.
Firm is the sky, firm is the earth; may the firm abide among the firm things.
RvKh 2.7.4b: O Agni, come toward us; bestow upon us unpraised wealth and nourishment. RvKh 2.7.5a: O great god Agni, speak for us to Mitra and to the gods; [speak] the favor of heaven and earth.
RvKh 2.8.1a: May there be union in me; do not strike me down, O wise one, nor the sovereign ruler.
O Jātavedas, grant us what is fitting for life; purify me.
May the mortal who seeks to harm us not destroy us, like one who has fallen from his chariot.
O Radiant One, we have awakened your watchfulness and your inspired thought.

RvKh 2.8.3a: Let the cows be free from disease; may he who possesses a good embryo release them. RvKh 2.8.3b: Whatever enemies there may be, and even those who act with pride against our patrons, let them be overcome.
RvKh 2.8.4a: O Jātavedas, bestow upon us the increase of wealth; purify me.

RvKh 2.8.4b: May the cows be our delight, many in the stall, dripping with ghee. RvKh 2.8.5a: O Agni, great as Mitra, call hither to us the gods, O god, and the favor of heaven and earth. RvKh 2.9.1a: May the Maruts flow together, and likewise their horses and men.
RvKh 2.9.1b: Whatever abundance there is of grain, that I offer with the flowing oblation.
RvKh 2.9.2a: May the cattle come here—those which have passed away, those whose companion Vāyu has rejoiced in.
RvKh 2.9.2b: Tvaṣṭṛ knows their various forms; may Savitṛ protect them in this world.
RvKh 2.9.3a: May the cattle flow together into this pen; may Bṛhaspati lead them here, knowing the way.
RvKh 2.9.3b: Sinīvālī leads them at the front; O Anumati, guide those who have arrived. RvKh 2.9.4a: I pour together the milk of the cows, along with the strength and essence of the clarified butter.
RvKh 2.9.4b: May our heroes be well-sprinkled; may the cows remain steadfast with their owner.
RvKh 2.9.5a: I bring the milk of the cows; I bring the essence of the grain.
RvKh 2.10.1a: May your male embryo enter the womb, like an arrow into a quiver.
RvKh 2.10.1b: May a hero be born here; may a son of ten months be born to you. RvKh 2.10.2a: I perform for you the rite pertaining to Prajāpati; may the embryo enter your womb.
RvKh 2.10.3a: May a male son be born to you; may a male be born after him.
Whatever auspicious seeds our bull begets for us—may that bull beget those same auspicious seeds for you.
Through them, may you give birth to a son; may he be born as the most heroic among his own kin.
The embryo that is in the barren cow, and that which she miscarries—Indra has placed that in the tree. Through those [seeds], may you find sons; be a prolific milch-cow.
May your minds be in harmony, may your intentions be in harmony, and may everything be in harmony.

RvKh 2.10.6b: I shall bind you with the tether of desire, so that there shall be no release. RvKh 2.10.7a: O Desire, may it be fulfilled for me; may it be truly unconquered for me. RvKh 2.11.1a: Let Agni go forth as the first of the deities; may he release her offspring from the snare of death.

May King Varuṇa grant his approval for this, so that this woman shall not weep over the misfortune of losing a grandson. May Agni, the lord of the household, protect her; may he extend her offspring and grant her long life. May she have an unfailing lap; may she live as a mother and experience the joy of seeing her grandson.

RvKh 2.11.3a: Let no terrible spirit rise up in your house at night; let those who weep settle elsewhere than with you. RvKh 2.11.3b: Do not, O woman with disheveled hair, beat your breast; as one whose son lives, shine forth in the world of your husband, rejoicing and beholding your offspring. RvKh 2.11.4a: [Drive away] childlessness, the mortality of grandchildren, evil, and even sin.
Like offspring, loosen yourself; from my enemies, I cast off the fetters.
With the god-ordained, perfecting *brāhmaṇa*, I strike down the *piśācas* who dwell in the womb.
I cast downward the flesh-eating deaths; may your sons live a long life.
Sight and hearing, mind and speech, the out-breath and the in-breath—this body is the physical frame.
These two downward-turned, forward-moving emissions, I consider this to be the ten-fold mechanism, the fountainhead.
The chest and the back, the hands and the arms, the shanks and the thighs, the belly and the head.
Hair, flesh, blood, bone, and marrow—this body is like a bubble on the water.
The two eyebrows, the forehead, as well as the ears, the jaws, the cheeks, and the chin;
the lips, the teeth, and likewise the tongue—this is my body, a jewel-treasury of the mouth.

The auspicious ones carry us across; ask this word of yours: who has approached that meeting-place and can say, "This is it"? The wife is the sign, the *parisrut* is the sign, and Bhāratī is the speaker of sacred knowledge.
RvKh 2.13.2b: Of those who are of one mind, the great-born one shall say, "He indeed is this.
RvKh 2.13.3a: Indra—what [is he] but the all-pervading Lord whom he shall consume with his splendor?
RvKh 2.13.3b: By him he caused the sun to shine, by whom these two worlds, heaven and earth, [were illumined].
O Agni Aṅgiras, take pleasure in Medhyātithi, the descendant of Kaṇva.
May the most excellent honeyed draught of the pressed soma not hold you back.
O Agni Aṅgiras, shine forth as the one most beloved by the gods.
With most peaceful and supremely auspicious protections, they have established peace and well-being for us.
May the divine Parjanya rain down upon us with a thunderous roar; may the plants flourish together.
May Heaven and Earth grant peace to our offspring; may there be peace for our bipeds and peace for our quadrupeds.
O Sleep, in this matter of sleep, lull all the people to rest.
Put others to sleep until the sun rises; may I remain awake until dawn.
There is a great serpent named Ajagara, who is fat and devoid of poison.
For in him the serpent is well-placed; by him we lull you to sleep.
The serpent, the serpent, the python, the butter-like, the great one who is without poison— from that serpent the rivers flow; may we find a firm footing in it.
The serpent named Kālika possesses the strength of nine thousand nāgas;
he was born in the pool of the Yamunā, and he is the vehicle of Nārāyaṇa.
RvKh 2.14.5a: If there is danger from a messenger of *kāla* (Time/Death), or if there is danger from *kāhakālika*.
RvKh 2.14.6a: Come, O Indra, by the paths invoked with praise; enjoy this our sacrifice as your allotted portion.
RvKh 2.14.6b: They have offered it satisfied, like a maiden to her maternal uncle, like the sacrificial fat of a father’s sister’s son—this is your portion.

He became a sovereign king, bringing glory, strength, and lordship; he was the master of a multitude of elephants and horses, a constant source of auspiciousness for men, and possessed long life. As for the serpent named Karkoṭaka, he is said to have venom in his very glance.
RvKh 2.14.8b: That serpent’s nature is "sarpatva" (the state of a gliding one); to that serpent, let there be homage to you! RvKh 2.14.9(1)a:
Of the exceedingly long-lasting and fierce [serpent], Viṣṇu, with his gentle aspect—[O Kālika!].
RvKh 2.14.9(1)b: Along the Yamunā river, O Kālika, I recollect your hymn of praise, O Viṣṇu! [O Kālika!]
Those who are in that luminous realm of heaven, or those who are in the rays of the sun—their seat has been prepared in the waters; homage to those serpents!
Homage be to the serpents, whoever they may be, who dwell upon the earth.
RvKh 2.14.10b: To those serpents who are in the intermediate space and those who are in heaven, homage!
RvKh 2.14.11a: Those with fierce weapons, the harassers, the great heroes, the masters of illusion, the powerful ones, seeking their prey.
RvKh 2.15: He whose ordinance the waters abide by, and under whose ordinance all cattle move.
RvKh 2.15: I invoke for protection Sarasvat, under whose ordinance abides the nourishment of the birds.
RvKh 2.16.1a: Speak forth, O female frog; announce the rain, O Tāduri!
RvKh 2.16.1b: Swim in the middle of the lake, having seized your four feet!
