*.abhi.*—Praskaṇva [composed] the *pragātha*; *pra*—Puṣṭigu; *yathā*—Śruṣṭigu; *yathā āyuḥ upamam*—Medhya; *etat te*—Mātariśvan; the second *pragātha* is addressed to the Viśvedevas; *bhūri*—Kṛśa; the praise of the gift of Pṛṣadhra; it is in the *gāyatrī* meter; however, the third and fifth verses are *anuṣṭubh*s; *prati*—Pṛṣadhra; ending in the *paṅkti* meter; the deities are indicated by their characteristic marks (*saliṅga-ukta*); *tvam ekā*—the *pāvamānī*s; six [verses] are addressed to the Viśvedevas; the last and the first are *pāvamānī* praises; the fifth is a *triṣṭubh*; *iḍā eva*—two [verses] of Bṛhaddiva; *yatra*—three [verses]; *sasruṣīḥ ekā ihi mama*—d.

The thirty-second [verse] is addressed to Prajāpati; the [verse] concerning the heart is addressed to the Viśvedevas. This is a blessing for the purpose of marriage. It is in the Ānuṣṭubh meter; the first [verse] is a Triṣṭubh; the twenty-third, twenty-fifth, tenth, and the *pra-uṣṇih* (or *puroṣṇih*) are Paṅktis;
the twelfth and the first two are Āstārapaṅkti and Prastārapaṅkti; the nineteenth is a Bṛhatī; the twenty-ninth is a Triṣṭubh; and the [thirtieth] is like a Jagatī.

Eight [verses] have *parāg* as their final word; one has *dhruva*; one has *eka*; one has *ud*; one has *yad ca asau*; two have *brahma*; ten are *vāmadevya*; one is addressed to Nakula; one is a *saurī* (addressed to Sūrya); one is a *gharma-stuti* (praise of the Gharma vessel); one is addressed to Bṛhaspati; one is addressed to Savitṛ; one is an *aṣṭi*; and one follows the Gharma. These remaining verses are addressed to Sūrya and Candra, and they are all in the *jagatī* meter.
Sing forth to Indra, the most bountiful, as he is known to be—him who, being Maghavan and rich in many treasures, bestows gifts upon his singers as if by the thousands.
Like one with a hundred armies, he advances boldly; he slays the Vṛtras for the sake of the donor. Like the streams from a mountain, the gifts of him who possesses much to enjoy overflow.
O Indra, lover of songs, may the pressed Soma drops, which are intoxicating, come to you.

O wielder of the thunderbolt, like waters filling a lake that is their home, they fill you for the sake of your bounty, O hero. Drink this which is peerless, furthering, exhilarating, great, and most sweet.
Just as you, being exhilarated, scatter [wealth] upon us, so do you boldly bestow it yourself like small grains of dust.
RvKh 3.1.5a: Thinking of you, we hasten toward this hymn with our prayer, like a horse toward its groomers.
RvKh 3.1.5b: O self-dependent Indra, the milch-cows provide for you what the *kaṇva*s offer as gifts.
RvKh 3.1.6a: With reverence, we sit near the mighty hero, the one of vast power whose wealth is inexhaustible.
Like a well being filled, O wielder of the thunderbolt, the inspired hymns flow forth for you,
O Indra. Whether it be now, or at the sacrifice,
or upon the earth— from there, O great-minded one, come to our sacrifice with your swift, fierce, and exalted steeds.
RvKh 3.1.8a: Those swift bay steeds of yours, fleet as the winds, who rush forward impetuously— RvKh 3.1.9a: For so much of this boon consisting of cattle, O Indra, we entreat you.
As you helped Etaśa in the decisive contest for wealth, as you helped Vaśa in Daśavraja; as you helped Kaṇva, O Maghavan, and Trasadasyu, so help Paktha in Daśavraja.
Just as you were with Gośarya and Ṛjiśvan, O Indra, so may you be possessed of cattle and gold for us.
Worship the far-famed Śakra, the bounteous giver,
for our protection—
he who bestows desirable wealth upon the one who presses the soma and praises him, as if with a thousandfold gift.
His arrows have a hundred points and are difficult to withstand; great are the powers of Indra.
Like Śini, he bestows abundance upon the generous patrons when the pressed juices have exhilarated him.
When the pressed drops, the Indus, have exhilarated him who is dear to them.
RvKh 3.2.3b: Like waters, the libation has been established for me; O Vasu, it flows like a milch-cow toward the worshipper.
RvKh 3.2.4a: For you, the invoker who calls for aid, free from malice, the inspired thoughts flow like honey.
RvKh 3.2.4b: O Vasu, the Soma drops, being invoked, have been placed by those who praise you within the hymns.

O Soma, you of good sacrifice, coming hither like a courser, you hasten toward us. O self-powerful one, when your songs of praise celebrate your self-power, you take pleasure in the invocation of the worshipper. 3 [He has sent forth] the fierce hero, the distributor, the winner of wealth, the lord of great and abundant bounty.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, like a well from a depth, you have ever swelled with wealth for the donor.
Whether you are now in a distant place, or on the earth, or in heaven— O Indra, great-souled one, fierce and exalted, harnessing your two bay steeds, come hither!
RvKh 3.2.8a: Your bay steeds, swift as chariot-borne, who are unfailing, surpass even the vigor of the wind.
RvKh 3.2.8b: With them you strike down the Dāsya of Manu, with them you roar aloud, and with them you encompass the sun.
RvKh 3.2.9a: O Vasu, O Hero, may we recognize from you such new [deeds] as these.
RvKh 3.2.9b: Just as you protected Medhyātithi, O Maghavan, and Nipātithi in the contest for wealth;
RvKh 3.2.10a: Just as you [protected] Kaṇva at the sacrifice and the rite, O Maghavan, in the long-continued dwelling of Damūnas;
RvKh 3.3.1a: Just as you drank the pressed Soma, O Indra, from the vessel of Saṃvaraṇa at the sacrifice.
RvKh 3.3.1b: O Maghavan, you were present with Nipātithi, Medhyātithi, Puṣṭigu, and Śruṣṭigu.
RvKh 3.3.2a: Pārṣadvāna established Praskaṇva; he raised up the aged Jivri who had been cast down. RvKh 3.3.2b: That seer obtained thousands of cattle from you, and so did Dasyave-vṛka.

RvKh 3.3.3a: To him who does not find satisfaction in hymns, yet who is conscious and the impeller of seers— RvKh 3.3.3b: speak toward that Indra with a new prayer, as one might [speak] to a liberal giver for his enjoyment. RvKh 3.3.4a: To whom they have sung the seven-headed hymn, three-layered, in the highest station.
He has roared across all these worlds; then indeed was manly power born.
We invoke that Indra who is the giver of riches to us;
for we know his most recent favor, may we go to a stall full of cattle. //5//
RvKh 3.3.6a: O Vasu, he for whom you strive to grant a gift attains the increase of wealth.
RvKh 3.3.6b: As such, O Maghavan Indra, lover of songs, we, having pressed the Soma, invoke you.
RvKh 3.3.7a: Never are you barren; O Indra, you do not fail the donor.
O Maghavan, ever more and ever again is thy divine bounty heaped up.
He who has reached out with his might, making Krivi tremble and striking down Śuṣṇa with his weapons—
when he propped up and spread out those heavens, then indeed was the son of the earth born.
RvKh 3.3.9a: He whose every Aryan and Dāsa is a friend, a protector of treasures, and an ally— RvKh 3.3.9b: even across the Aryan Ruśama, for you, O Pavīru, that wealth is being prepared.
RvKh 3.3.10a: The swift, honey-sweet, ghee-dripping sages have sung their hymn of praise.
O Śakra, just as you drank the pressed soma in the house of Vivasvat Manu;
just as you, O Indra, took pleasure in Trita through your desire, and you rejoice together with Āyu;
O Indra, you rejoiced when the soma was pressed for Pṛṣadhra, Mātariśvan, and Mādhya.
As [you drank] Soma from Daśaśipra, from Daśoṇya,
from Syūmaraśmi, and from Ṛjīṣin;
he who established the hymns as his own and who boldly drank the Soma.

For whomsoever Viṣṇu strode out three steps according to the ordinances of Mitra; for whomsoever you, O Indra, have taken pleasure in the hymns, O powerful one, O lord of a hundred powers, in the contest for booty— for him we invoke you, as those who milk a cow for its milk call a good milch-cow, and for the sake of glories.
He who is our giver is our father, the great, the fierce, the sovereign lord.
In his coming, the fierce Maghavan, rich in many treasures, bestows upon us cattle and horses.
O Vasu, he for whom you intend to grant a gift prospers with the increase of wealth.

Seeking wealth, we invoke Indra, the lord of wealth and master of a hundred powers, with our hymns of praise. Never do you neglect; you protect both lineages. O fourth Āditya, that immortal power of yours, the *savana*, has established itself in heaven.
O Maghavan, O Indra, lover of songs, you who grant aid, may you bestow your favor upon the worshipper;
O Vasu, hear our songs and our fair praise, and listen to our call as you did for Kaṇva. The ancient hymn has been recited; speak the sacred prayer to Indra.
Many lofty hymns of Truth have resounded; the inspired thoughts of the singer have been released.
Indra has shaken together vast riches, together the two worlds, and together the sun.
O you who are the highest among the wealthy and the greatest among the bulls!
O Maghavan Indra, we implore you, the greatest breaker of forts, the winner of cattle, the lord of wealth.
You who came to Kutsa and Atithigva, growing stronger day by day,
subduing them— we, seeking booty, invoke you, the Lord of Bay Steeds, the performer of a hundred deeds.
RvKh 3.5.3a: May the pressing-stones pour out for us the essence of the honey of all [the Soma-pressers].

RvKh 3.5.3b: Those drops which are pressed among people in the distance, and those which are pressed nearby— RvKh 3.5.4a: Strike down all hostilities and cast them away; let everyone press [Soma] for wealth.

Even when the exhilarating stalks of Soma are upon your head, there you are satisfied with the Soma. O Indra, come even closer with your aids that bring measured wisdom; come with your most peaceful protections, O most peaceful one; come with your sleep-inducing powers, O you who are well-sleeping.
Make him who conquers in battle, the lord of the virtuous, the protector of all people, a sharer of fortune among his progeny.
May those who offer hymns of praise extend their power through their deeds, purifying their will in due order.
May we be those who are most effective for your aid; may we be yours in the battles.
RvKh 3.5.7b: Having won through the invocations of the sacrificer and the calls to the gods, they have become renowned.
RvKh 3.5.8a: For I, O Lord of the Bay Steeds, desiring booty, ever go to the contest with my prayers and invocations for you.
RvKh 3.6.1a: This heroic power of yours, O Indra, the poets celebrate with their songs.
They sang their praises; they brought forth strengthening food dripping with clarity. Having spread abroad, they reached him with their prayers.
They have approached Indra for protection through their good deeds—those at whose pressed juices you take delight.
As you were exhilarated at Saṃvarta and as you were at Kṛśa, so, O Indra, be exhilarated among us.
O all you gods, come to us together in harmony;
O Vasus and Rudras, come to us for our protection; may the Maruts hear our call.
May Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī, and the seven rivers favor my invocation.

O Indra, whatever wealth you possess, O most bountiful one among the generous; O Lord of the assembly, O Lord of men, you indeed are our portion of strength, O you of noble will. Through our priestly offices and invocations of the gods, we consider ourselves as those who have won the prize.
RvKh 3.6.7a: For the noble blessings of the people and Indra’s life-force exist.
RvKh 3.6.7b: Come to us, O Maghavan, for our protection; milk out for us swelling nourishment. RvKh 3.6.8a:
May we worship you, O Indra, with hymns; you, O Śatakratu, belong to us.
Great indeed is the heroic power of Indra; it has been manifested as he advances.
O Dasyave-vṛka, this is your gift.
A hundred white oxen shine like stars in the sky.
By his greatness, he has stood firm like a pillar.
A hundred bamboos, a hundred dogs, a hundred skins of *mlāta*—
a hundred tufts of *balbaja* grass, four hundred ruddy ones, for me.
O Kaṇvāyanas, you are well-disposed, moving from strength to strength; like horses, you do not falter. Then indeed they celebrated the sevenfold [sacrifice] and the full, great glory.
O Dasyave-vṛka, your gift has been seen, which is bold and shameless; its power is as vast as the sky in its extent. Dasyave-vṛka, whose will is purified, gave ten thousand to me.
RvKh 3.8.2b: He bestowed wealth day after day. RvKh 3.8.3a: A hundred donkeys are mine, and a hundred woolly sheep.
RvKh 3.8.4a: There, too, Pūtakratāyī was led forth clearly.
Like one of the herd of horses;
Agni has been perceived, the wise bearer of oblations, he whose chariot is accompanied by the Maruts.
Agni, with his bright luster, has shone forth mightily like Sūrya in heaven; Sūrya has shone forth in heaven.
RvKh 3.9.1a: O Maghavan, you stood by the drop as it fought with the bow at the Aṃśumatī river.
RvKh 3.9.1b: O Hero Indra, you are the winner of waters and riches; those are your many deeds of victory, O performer of much.
RvKh 3.10.1a: For the Pāvamānī verses bring well-being, yield easily, and drip with clarity like clarified butter.
The essence gathered by the seers, immortality placed within the Brāhmaṇas—
may the purifying verses (pāvamānī) point out this world to us, as well as that world beyond. May these goddesses, brought together with the gods, fulfill our desires.
RvKh 3.10.3a: With that purifier with which the gods always purify themselves, RvKh 3.10.3b: with that thousand-streamed one, may the *pāvamānī* verses purify me.
RvKh 3.10.4a: The purifier belonging to Prajāpati has a hundred supports.
Golden.
With it, we who know the Brahman purify the pure Brahman.
May Indra purify me with good guidance; may Soma with well-being, and Varuṇa with concord.
May King Yama purify me with the *pramṛṇā* [verses]; may Jātavedas purify me with the *ūrjayantī* [verse].
The *pāvamānī* verses are auspicious; by means of them one goes to Nandana, and one partakes of holy foods.

And he attains immortality. (RvKh 3.10.1) Whatever terrible sin was mine while dwelling in the womb, or whatever else occurred when I was being born; whatever word of mine was not performed by my mother and father; and whatever has become stationary or moving—[may all that be removed]. (RvKh 3.10.2)
RvKh 3.10.2b: Whatever word of mine has been uttered in joy, that I purify with the *pāvamānī* verses.
RvKh 3.10.3ab: From buying and selling, from the defect of one's birth, from what is eaten, from what is fit to be eaten, and from accepting gifts;
and even from eating with those who should not be fed—that cruelty I purify with the *pāvamānī* verses.
Whatever sin arises from killing a cow, from theft, from the murder of a woman, or from evil conduct—
that I purify with these *pāpavānī* [verses].
From the killing of a Brahmin, from drinking liquor, from stealing gold, or from sexual union with a low-caste woman—

RvKh 3.10.5b: And from approaching the wife of a guru, I purify myself by means of these *pāvamānī* verses. RvKh 3.10.6ab: From killing children, from the murder of mother and father, from [stealing] earth, from theft, from sexual intercourse with women of all castes, and from accepting gifts from the wicked—these [verses] instantly strike away all that evil deed; I purify myself by means of these *pāvamānī* verses.
Whatever food is offered without a mantra into the consumer of oblations (the fire),
and whatever sin has been committed during the year— that I purify with the *pāvamānī* verses.
Whatever was poorly sacrificed, poorly recited, or whatever evil was done through ignorance— [that I purify].
Those who have not sacrificed and those unworthy of sacrifice—those I purify with the *pāvamānī* verses.

The wombs of *ṛta*, the abodes of immortality, all possessing holy fragrance for the gods—may those waters carry away our evil. I go with faith to the world of the righteous; that I purify with the *pāvamānī* verses.
RvKh 3.10.10ab: [This corresponds to verse 5 of the manuscript.
RvKh 3.10.11–14: [These correspond to verses 1–4 of the manuscript; 15 corresponds to the aforementioned verse 6 of the manuscript.
RvKh 3.10.16a: One who meditates upon the *pāvamānī* verses, the ancestors, the gods, and Sarasvatī...
He should offer milk, clarified butter, honey, and water to the ancestors of that [person].
But all the seers, desiring to conquer heaven, performed austerities;
indeed, one should mutter the *pāvamānī* verses, which are the foremost of all austerities.

Those wise ones who recite the *Pāvamāna* as the supreme Brahman shall become Brahmins for seven births, wealthy and masters of the Vedas. There are ten more [verses] than these, making six hundred *ṛc*s of the *Pāvamāna*.
Chanting this while offering oblations, one shall conquer even the terrible fear of death. The *pāvamāna* hymns are the supreme Brahman, the pure light, eternal.
One should worship the seers with milk, clarified butter, honey, and water.
May Iḍā herself attend you both with clarified butter, she whose station the seekers of the gods purify again and again.
RvKh 3.11.1b: Stepping in ghee, the Śakvarī, with Soma upon her back, she who belongs to all the gods has approached the sacrifice.
RvKh 3.11.2a: The goddess belonging to all the gods, purifying herself, has come, in whom these many [beings] dwell.
With her who has broad backs,
rejoicing in the communal feasts, may we be masters of riches.
Where those who have abandoned the body, having conquered through faith and austerity, attain the worlds;
where the great-souled gods, together with Indra and the hosts of Maruts, reside.
RvKh 3.12.2b: Where Brahmā and Viṣṇu are, there make me immortal; O Indu, flow around for Indra. RvKh 3.12.3a: Where that supreme station is, which is magnified in the world of Viṣṇu;
RvKh 3.12.3b: where the gods whose deeds are well-performed dwell, there make me immortal; O Indu, flow around for Indra.
RvKh 3.13.1a: Those waters that have flowed, flowing day and night—those very ones;
RvKh 3.13.1b: I, whose resolve is excellent, call upon the goddesses for their protection.
RvKh 3.14.1a: Come, O Indra, with your chariot rich in wealth; together you drank the Soma for exhilaration.
RvKh 3.14.1b: Having drunk from our hearts and being exhilarated with the Maruts, O wielder of the thunderbolt, come to the spread-out [sacrifice] for the slaying of Vṛtra.
RvKh 3.15.1a: I place my will within your heart; let your mind follow my mind. RvKh 3.15.1b: Delight in my word with single-minded devotion; may Bṛhaspati join you to me.
The Ordainer has given you to me; may the Ordainer bestow you upon me.
The Ordainer has handed you over to me; Anumati has granted you to me.
O Anumati, give your approval; O Svānumati, give your approval.

RvKh 3.15.3b: "For me, bring this together; let it be bound to me by speech, by sight, and by mind. RvKh 3.15.4ab: "I have drawn forth your heart; let that be my heart. And likewise, that which is my heart, let that be your heart."
With my heart I have grasped your heart; with my breath your breath. I grasp your eye with my eye; I grasp your mind with my mind.
Intent, thought, sight, hearing, and also strength— [I have grasped].
With that splendor which the gods have attained, I bind your mind. With this amulet made of food, with the variegated thread of breath,
bound with the knot of truth, I bind both your heart and your mind.
The turning toward you, the turning back,
and the enchantment of you— these both Indra and Agni, the two Aśvins, Tvaṣṭṛ, and Dhātṛ have fashioned.
With whatever thought you speak, or with whatever another seeks to harm you...
O Agni, bring all that to me; it is to be won for my servant. The forest-dweller, the well-born, the up-rising, the wood-dweller—may cattle enter into me; may the plants enter into me.
RvKh 3.15.11b: May the kings enter into me, just as I desire. RvKh 3.15.12a: May I have an ascent that is endless for you; may I be inseparable from my heart. RvKh 3.15.13a:
May the assembly and the gathering, both daughters of Prajāpati, protect us with one mind.
In the gathering places, at the beautiful step—homage indeed to Vaiśvānara!
(RvKh 3.15.13b) ...by that step he takes away your vital breaths;
and furthermore, he takes away that which is among other people as well. (RvKh 3.15.14ab)
I [take] your eye with my eye; I [take] your mind with my mind.
Your heart is struck down, your mind is struck down; your mind is struck down among others.
Among all those with black hair, your mind is struck down among others.
Look upon me and the sun, and never upon anyone else as a third. You are mindfulness, O Kāma, the arouser of desire; may desire for you arise within me.
That mind of yours which is desirable and has been fashioned in many ways throughout the worlds—[may it be fixed on me].

As rivers flow toward the ocean, we cause you to follow us entirely. I kindle your heart; like fire, we set it ablaze for me. This is your glowing coal in the heart; I am your flame—you are being consumed.
May the Ordainer restrain both your consciousness and your mind within me.
Your consciousness is dependent upon me; your mind attains union with me.
You have been turned toward me by me.
Your grace has perished in another; may your mind delight in me.
May your mind [be] in accordance [with me].
Sight, hearing, and all that has been studied—I take all that away from you. They placed that very thing, which perceives the goal, within these hearts;
it is all-knowing and all-seeing—may it accomplish our rites for us.

O Jātavedas, those [evil deeds] of the ill-intentioned man which have entered into thee as the fire of his ritual praise—I offer them as their allotted portion. May the gods satisfy me with all my desires. O singer, celebrate the well-restrained power of the heat of the Bhṛgus and the Aṅgirases.
And I cause your mind to turn back toward the descendants of Kuśika and those who are lower than them.
That mind of yours which is desirable and has been directed in many ways throughout the worlds— that we cause it to turn back for you, O Brahmin, both by day and by night.
RvKh 3.15.32a: That charm for reconciliation which Kakṣīvat, the son of the Aṅgirases, discovered.
RvKh 3.16.1a: Strike him out from his bed, O master of the house, away from his kinsmen!
RvKh 3.16.1b: Seizing him by the neck, make him rise; do not let him enter from the foot!
RvKh 3.16.2a: Let the Maruts rise up from the pit; let them draw [the water] from the ocean from here.
RvKh 3.16.2b: By his will may this Agni burn; by his will may Sūrya scorch. RvKh 3.16.3a: Just as you wither a woman who is tormented for the sake of a bed of love.
RvKh 3.16.3b: Thus, dry up our enemies; show favor to us by day and by night! RvKh 3.16.4a: O Mitra and Varuṇa, may this [speech] of mine be expanded by my thought.
RvKh 3.16.4b: Having given, having drunk, and having placed it at the forefront, [act] so that we shall be under your divine control in this world.
O Goddess Vaśā, drive the Dāsas far away, those who follow after [the enemy].
With the seasons and the seasonal periods, with life-force and with splendor,
with the brilliance of the year— purify me together with that!
By this sacred formula (*brahman*), O Agni, and by this Indra who is praised, [may we be purified].
Make him the sovereign king and supreme lord over his own people.
O Agni, strike down their joined arrows into every vital organ.
Drive the stake of *khadira* wood into the heart of our enemies; do not let it enter us.

Be firm and nourishing for me; Bṛhaspati has given you to me. With me as your husband, live a hundred autumns, blessed with offspring. Be not a widow for more than a hundred years, remaining steadfast in your vows.
May she be radiant and renowned, a lawful wife devoted to her husband.
May she give birth to many sons and never encounter suffering anywhere.
May your husband always be a drinker of Soma and ever dedicated to righteousness.
May you have eight sons, be fortunate, and remain devoted to your husband;
may you always delight the hearts of your husband, father, and brother,
just as Indrāṇī does for Indra and Śrī for Śrīdhara.
As Gaurī is to Śaṅkara, and likewise to her husband’s own father; as Anasūyā was to Atri, and Arundhatī to Vasiṣṭha;
and as Satī was to Kauśika—so may you be to your husband.
Agni is indeed one, though kindled in many ways; the Sun is one, pervading the entire universe.

He whom the officiating priests, acting in harmony, carry about as this sacrifice while fashioning him in many forms—he who sits yoked as a learned Brahmin, what indeed is the sacrificer’s awareness of him there?
RvKh 3.19.1a: Like birds from their dwelling, we have flown up; let the Bhr̥gus come, thinking [of us].
O Purūravas, go back again to your home, where the divine folk have led our mind to heaven.
RvKh 3.20: Whatever was left undone, whatever sin we have committed...
RvKh 3.20: May the plants protect him from that [evil], from misfortune, and from sin.

RvKh 3.21.1a: O Maruts, that army of our enemies which approaches us, vying with us in its might— RvKh 3.21.1b: Hide it in darkness devoid of holy law (ṛta), so that they may not recognize one another.
RvKh 3.21.2a: Let the enemies become blind, like headless serpents.
RvKh 3.22.1a: The Brahman, first born in the east, Vena has revealed from the horizon with his brilliant light.
RvKh 3.22.1b: He has disclosed its highest stations, the depths, and the womb of both the existent and the non-existent.

This royal power has gone to the Father, established in abundance for the first-born generation. For him they prepare this brightly shining, well-poured *gharma* for the first draught. Great, as soon as he was born, the Father propped apart the vast heaven and the earthly dwelling-place, the mid-air.
From the deep foundation, by his very birth, Bṛhaspati attained the formidable; he is the sovereign deity thereof.
Toward that god Savitṛ, between the two worlds, whose wisdom is that of a seer, whose lofty splendor has shone forth at his impulse.

O Sūryā and Candramas, you who best know the way, you two shine with great, wealthy splendor in heaven. Moving by means of the *sāman*, you move as the *sāman*-wanderers; the law (*vrata*) of those two gods can never be overcome.
Both traverse the two ends of the heavenly realm; like rays from the sky, they stretch out across the ocean.
Both, possessing the wisdom of a seer, become the two worlds; like the sun and moon, they move with their thoughts destroyed.
Both are the lords of heaven, the radiant knowers of all; both are the suns of the sky, both are the moons, far-seeing.
Both possess all boons and are sources of wide space; both are worthy of choice.
The two wise ones, of great vows,
protectors of all, furthering [our progress], crossing over [difficulties], finders of heaven, have become visible with their many rays.

Sūryā and Candrā are beautiful in their wealth; they are the six who are lovely to behold (or: they are the brilliant and lovely ones). The seven rivers bear his fame; Heaven and Earth and the broad land bear his lovely form.
For us, O Indra, the sun and the moon move in alternating succession for the sake of vision and for faith.

These two move one after the other by means of their creative power (*māyā*); like two playing children, they go around the sacrifice. One of them surveys all beings; the other, ordaining the seasons, is born again and again.
IV. Chapter (Table of Contents):

*Suśrī*, *Suvāk*, *Sarva*, *Hiraṇya*, and *Ātma-stuti*. The fifth, eighth, and ninth [verses] are *triṣṭubh*s; the seventh is a *śakvarī*. [The hymn] beginning with *bhūmiḥ* consists of seven verses addressed to Prajāpati; it is a praise of lac (*lākṣā*).—

*.Medhā.*: nine verses; *Medhā*, *Mānavī*, *Mādhavī*; the fourth verse and those following are *Mahābṛhatī*, *Paṅkti*, *Virāj*, *Jagatī*, *Gāyatrī*, and *Triṣṭubh*. *.Ā sūs.*: seven verses; *Atharvaṇa* is addressed to the *Subheṣaja* (Excellent Medicine) and is dedicated to Agni (*Āgneya*). The [verses] are the *Prakṛti*, *Kṛti*, *Ākṛti*, *Vikṛti*, *Saṃkṛti*, *Abhikṛti*, and *Utkṛti*. *.Venas.*: a triplet; *Vena* is the subject, and it concerns the state of being (*bhāva-vṛtta*). *.Yena.*: seven verses less one (six verses); *Mānava*, *Śivasankalpa*, and *Mānasa*. *.Yāsām.*: two verses, both *Anuṣṭubh* and *Paṅkti*. *.Nejameṣa.*: a triplet; *Nejameṣa* is dedicated to Prajāpati (*Prājāpatya*). *.Anīkavantam.*: one verse.
To him, for the feast of the gods, let the sons come together in unison—unassailable through inspired praise, bold for your renown. I move about with the Rudras and the Vasus. 1.1.1–3c.
O Night, you have filled the earthly realm with the abodes of your father;
great, you spread across the seats of heaven, and the brilliant darkness rolls forth.
O Night, those steeds of yours that gaze upon men—ninety-nine in number—are yoked.

RvKh 4.2.2b: May there be eighty, or eight, or even seventy-seven. RvKh 4.2.3ab: I take refuge in Night, the mother who is the dwelling place of all beings, the auspicious, blessed, dark one, the rest for the entire world.

I have entered the auspicious night, which brings rest, which binds [all things], and which is garlanded with planets and constellations; may we reach its blessed end. With a disciplined mind, I shall praise the Goddess, the refuge of all, who is dear to the followers of the Rigveda.
RvKh 4.2.5b: For Jātavedas, we shall press the Soma, which is difficult to attain and measured by a thousand [verses].
RvKh 4.2.6a: This was resorted to by the seers for the sake of the peace of the twice-born.
RvKh 4.2.6b: You have arisen within the Ṛgveda; as the Veda, you cast down those who act with hostility.
O Goddess, those Brahmins who take refuge in you, the carrier of oblations—
whether they possess little knowledge or great knowledge— may she carry us across all difficulties.
Those twice-born ones who shall proclaim you as fire-colored, auspicious, and gentle;
Agni carries one across difficulties as if crossing a river in a boat; he carries one beyond misfortunes.

In difficult places, on uneven ground, in terrible situations, in the perils of battle with enemies, during fires, robberies, and falls, and for the warding off of evil planetary influences—*om*, salutations to the warder-off of evil planetary influences! *Om namas*.

In difficult places, on uneven ground, in battles, and in forests, having caused them to be deluded, they fall [upon me]. Grant me freedom from fear; grant me freedom from fear. Om, homage! Keśinī is the name of all beings, and Pañcamī is her name as well.

RvKh 4.2.11b: May that goddess of the quarters protect me every year on every side; may she protect me on every side. Om, obeisance! RvKh 4.2.12b: I take refuge in the goddess Durgā. Obeisance to Sutarasī, to Tarasī; obeisance to Sutarasī, to Tarasī. RvKh 4.2.13a: In difficult places, [may] Durgā [protect us]; may the goddesses grant us peace for our well-being.
Whoever should always recite this meritorious hymn to Rātri night after night—
[this] *Rātrisūkta*, which is in the Gāyatrī meter, composed by Kuśika Saubhara or by Rātri Bhāradvājī, and which is appropriate for that specific time— one should recite it constantly.
RvKh 4.3.1a: From yonder we invoke Indra hitherward—he who wins cattle, wins wealth, and wins horses.
RvKh 4.4.1a: Homage be to the lightning; homage be to the thunder. RvKh 4.4.1b:
Homage be to the stone that you hurl at me as one who is difficult to overcome.
Homage to you, O Son of the Slopes, since you gather together fervor.
Be gracious to our bodies; grant safety to our cattle.
O Son of the Slopes, let there be homage indeed to you; we offer homage to your weapon and to your heat.
We know your supreme name, which is hidden in secret; you are placed even within the ocean.

You whom the gods have brought forth—conceiving this prayer, may you grant us strength for the winning of booty. As such, being praised in our assembly, be gracious to us; homage be to you, O Goddess! 4.4.4b–d. RvKh_4,4.4b: sā no mṛḍa vidathe gṛṇānā tasyai te namo astu devi //4//

The cruel sorcery which our enemies fashion for us, like a bride, that we drive away with a sacred prayer; let it return to the one who performed it. [That sorcery] which possesses a head, possesses ears, has every form, and causes fear.
RvKh 4.5.2b: "I have sent you forth today; now yoke yourself with the horses.
RvKh 4.5.3a: "With whatever mind you speak words that are adverse and harmful," RvKh 4.5.4a: "Turn back toward your maker; you have been cast out by us with might."
Return his life and progeny to this man, O Puruṣādini!
O Kṛtyā, go back to him who fashioned you here; return to your source. Destroy the enemies, the sorceries, and all the malevolent spirits. //5//
O Kṛtyā, return quickly to the very house of the one who sent you!
Destroy his cattle and utterly ruin his heroic sons!
He who approaches you, O Kṛtyā...
He who has joined together your limbs with his wisdom, like the *Ṛbhu* of a chariot—go to him;
there is your people, that people who do not know you.
Or perhaps someone else is harming you.
Like a blazing fire to a tree, touch his body as you are provoked;
O *kṛtyā*,
let there be no head left for that evildoer, and let your own heat consume him entirely.

O Goddess, by those paths of ours which are auspicious and lead away to the distant realm, send our enemies and sorceries there; turn them back. Whoever, as an enemy or a hater, seeks to harm us even with his mind—
Whether you stand far away or near, drink the heart-blood of that person by whom you have been sent as a magical missile (*kṛtyā*),
with evil intent, desiring to kill us.
Let the autumn thunderbolt destroy both his open and his hidden [parts].

Whether you go to us as a two-footed one, or whether you go as a four-footed one—from there, O lawless one, we have cast you out; may you enter the eight-footed house of the doer. He who curses us when we do not curse, and he who curses us when we do curse—
Like a tree struck by lightning, let him fall from the very root.
Him whom we hate, and he who hates us— the malevolent one who curses us—
I hurl back at him for death, like a piece of meat thrown to a dog.
Whatever curse there is from a rival wife, and whatever curse from a sister;
and whatever a Brahmin, when enraged, may curse—make all that lie beneath our feet. Whether he be a kinsman or a stranger, whoever seeks to harm us—[make him lie beneath our feet].
Trampling upon him, shatter his head; it shall swell until it bursts. Advance toward the thousand-eyed one, having yoked the swift chariot of the curse.
Seeking out the enemies like a she-wolf entering an unbarred house.
May you ward off our curses, like Agni burning down a pen;
strike down our enemies like a thunderbolt strikes a celestial tree. O Proṣṭha, drive away my enemies, the curses, the sorceries, and those [enemies] who are dear to my heart.
Those who are crooked, smooth-tongued, and evil-hearted [go] toward the kindled Jātavedas.
Make us free from rivals in the east; make us auspicious in the south. Depart, O sorcery! Do not stay; lead us away like the footprint of one who has grown old.
For you are the enemy of the beast; therefore, you ought to strike him down. O you of terrible form, of excellent form, O destroyer within the mouth of the inviolable cow!
Having seized this wondrous thing yourself, take hold of those who have been paralyzed.
You are Indra, Yama, and Varuṇa; you are the waters, Agni, and also Anila.
You are Brahmā, Rudra, Tvaṣṭṛ, and Prajāpati.
Turn hither, turn back! O seasons and years!
The days and nights, the years, and the cardinal and intermediate directions are yours for me.
You are Indra, Yama, and Varuṇa; you are the waters, Agni, and also Vāyu.
Anointed and well-adorned, do you destroy all our evil.
And recognize those men of evil intent who perform *kṛtyā* rites.
Just as a person repeatedly kills with an arrow one who has already been struck by a sword,
so may we, joined with you as our ally, destroy his standing and moving possessions alike.
Arise, go away from here; O cow-slayer, what do you seek here? I shall cut off your necks and your feet as well, O Kṛtyā; run away!
Our swords are made of good steel, and we know your very joints.
RvKh 4.5.33b: You are those who strike down; O fierce ones, if you [would] make us live, [then do so]. RvKh 4.5.34a: Do not leave behind of him anything two-footed, nor anything four-footed.
RvKh 4.5.35a: [The arrow] sent by one acting as an enemy, with which [he aims] in whatever manner...
RvKh 4.5.35b: Then let that which dwells within me likewise impel you.
RvKh 4.5.36a: Thus have you been humiliated by us, O Goddess, through our sacred word (*brahman*) in every way.
RvKh 4.5.36b: Having made him who has taken refuge [in you] so, strike us down as one who removes evil.
May all the gods strike him down; may the Veda be my inner armor. Just as a tree struck by lightning withers away from its very roots, so shall he wither who seeks to do me evil.
Just as one who has been struck down runs back toward that very person,
so let evil run toward him who desires to do me harm.
O Vimatha, crush Kuvīra, Sukha, Rudra, and Nandīmāna!
Granting long life, bestowing luster, increasing wealth, and breaking through obstacles—
may this golden ornament, full of splendor, enter into me for the sake of victory.
High-spirited, a conqueror in battle, triumphant in the assembly, and a winner of wealth.
RvKh 4.6.2b: All prosperities, gathered together in their entirety, are contained within this gold.
RvKh 4.6.3a: With good fortune, I have grasped the name of gold, as if it were that of my own father.
RvKh 4.6.3b: By means of it, O Sūrya, I have made my skin dear to men.
The sovereign ruler and the wide-ruling king, the favor that is mine and steadfast,
the fortune that is at the head of the kingdom— with that, O Indra, unite me. O Agni, that gold which was born from the offspring of the gods, the immortal that was produced among mortals—

What Varuṇa, the king of the Vedas, knows, and what the goddess Sarasvatī knows, and what Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, knows— that splendor may it grant me for long life. Neither the *rakṣases* nor the *piśācas* overcome that, for it is the first-born power of the gods.

He who wears the gold of the Dākṣāyaṇas secures long life among the gods; he secures long life among men. Therefore, I bind this upon myself for a hundred autumns, so that I may be long-lived and reach old age. This gold, drawn from clarified butter, is honey-sweet, wealth-conquering, sustaining, and enduring.
Making my rivals in debt and casting them down, ascend me for great good fortune! Make me dear among the gods; make me dear among kings;
bestow splendor upon splendor within me, who am dear to all protectors.
The earth is your mother, the sky is your father, and Aryaman is your grandfather.
You are indeed named Ghṛtācī; you are the sister of the gods.
Whoever drinks you lives, for you protect that person.
RvKh 4.7.2b: You are the protector of the eternal ones, the uniter of the eternal ones.

RvKh 4.7.3a: Whatever has been done with the staff, whatever with the arrow, or whatever by the heat of Varuṇa’s wrath— RvKh 4.7.3b: Of that you are the remedy; having applied the remedies upon the surface, [heal] the plants.
Tree after tree you fly; like trees, as it were, does the maiden appear. Victorious and standing firm, you are indeed named Saṃjeyā.
Stand firm upon the auspicious *plakṣa*, the *aśvattha*, the *khadira*, and the *dhuva*.
RvKh 4.7.5b: On the auspicious leaf of the *nyagrodha* tree, that Arundhatī has seized me.
RvKh 4.7.6a: You fall upon the blood of the horse; you tread upon that leaf. RvKh 4.7.7a: O golden-leaved, fortunate one, you are unswerving (or: subtle).
O you with hairy breasts!
You are the sister of the waters, O Lakṣmī; Vāta has indeed become your soul.
Night is your mother, the cloud is your father, and Aryaman is your grandfather.
RvKh 4.7.1b: Or you are the name of the stone and so forth; you are the sister of the gods. RvKh 4.7.2a: He who drinks you lives; you protect the man. RvKh 4.7.2b:
You are the supporter of all things, the one who leads all things downward.
Of that [tree], you are the healing one; your name is Niṣkṛti (Expiation).
You stand auspiciously upon the *prakṣa*, the *aśvattha*, the *khadira*, and the *dhava* tree. You are auspicious on the *nyagrodha* and the *parṇa* tree; do not lead me away, O Arundhatī!
You climb from tree to tree like a maiden longing for a bridegroom; victorious and standing firm, you are the one named Saṃjayā. O golden-hued, youthful, vigorous one, you who consume the hair!

O *lākṣā*, you are the sister of the waters, since you became restless when moved by the wind. O golden-armed one, auspicious one, sun-colored one, most beautiful one, you go toward the cosmic order (*ṛta*); prepare it! Prepare this manly power!
O son of an unmarried woman, you who are tawny, do not become the father of one named Ghṛtācī. This horse is the fame of Yama; let them sprinkle it with his bone.
That which fell from the horse's bone dried upon a leaf.
RvKh 4.7.9b: Sadāpatatnī asi; mā nehi Arundhatī.
RvKh 4.7.10a: Ghṛtācakre vāmarate vidyutparṇe Arundhatī.
RvKh 4.7.10b: Yā turaṃgameṣṭā asi, tvam aṅga niṣkarīyasī.
Whatever of yours was consumed by the Piśācas while you were awake, let that be restored again even now.
Let the lac, or whatever is a universal remedy, protect us together with the gods.
The Aṅgirasas have given me wisdom; the Seven Seers have given me wisdom.
May Indra and Agni, and may Dhātṛ, bestow wisdom upon me.
May King Varuṇa grant me wisdom; may the goddess Sarasvatī grant me wisdom.
O Aśvins, the two gods adorned with lotus-garlands, bestow wisdom upon me.
That wisdom which is among the Apsarases and that mind which is among the Gandharvas—
may that divine and human wisdom enter into me here.
May that which has been spoken by my mind find delight; may I be able to recite what I proclaim.
May I perceive what has been perceived, and may what has been heard abide within me.
May I be united with the sacred vow; may we be gathered together with the *brahman*.
O far-seeing one, my body [is restored]; my speech yields honey.
May this sun increase me; you are the spokes of the wheel of sacred knowledge (*brahman*).
O goddess Medhā, who trembles with the mind and is beloved by the Gandharvas, be gracious to us in return.
Speak wisdom for me; speak prosperity for me. May I become wise, agile, and active.
To the wonderful Lord of the Assembly, the beloved and desirable friend of Indra— May I be wise, well-minded, fair-faced, faithful in thought, true in intellect, and most gracious.
May I, possessing great glory and being steadfast, become an expounder of this through the application of its sovereign power.
That wisdom which the hosts of gods and the ancestors revere—
may Agni, the lord of the household, of beautiful countenance and radiant splendor, come from afar like the sun.
Having perceived Agni as the light upon the earth,
bring him hither— he who, having come upon the path, shakes off all adversaries.
Having stepped upon the earth, O steed, seek Agni with your luster.
RvKh 4.9.2: May Agni, our steadfast messenger, the bearer of oblations, bring the gods from heaven and earth to our sacrifice.
He is the inspired priest, the consecrated envoy, the worshipful one worthy of sacrifice, the seer.
As Apnavāna did, as Aurva did, as Bhṛgu did, and as Jamadagni did...

Agni, your bull, smoke-bannered, awakening at dawn—Vaiśvānara has looked upon the forefront of the dawns; the prize-winning steed, the giver of wealth, has stepped across toward us. May we dig up Agni Vaiśvānara, the one of beautiful countenance, from the earth where the well-doers have made a fair world for themselves, as we ascend to this celestial vault. Then, through your nourishment, O Nourisher, restore to us what was lost, and restore to us our wealth once more.

A fat man, self-restrained, crying out loudly, does not indeed satisfy the gods when he fails to impel them toward the quarters. O Agni, I think of you; O Agni, you are the pure upholder of vows. O Agni, bring the gods here to our sacrifice and to our oblation.
Bearing the sacred laws, the protector of vows, undeceived, worship the gods for us—you who are ageless and rich in heroes.
Bestowing jewels, O benevolent Agni, protect us so that we may live, O Jātavedas!

RvKh 4.9.6: May the god Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, the possessor of good wealth, the delightful sage, whose thoughts are true, the sacrificing priest, the invoker of all invokers—O Agni, those gods whom you have sacrificed to and whom you have gratified, who rejoiced in your office as Hotṛ—send this sacrifice, together with the sacrificial portions that have been won and which go to the gods, to heaven among the gods. And may Agni Sviṣṭakṛt be the Hotṛ; for the winning of wealth and the granting of treasure, accept this word of homage. RvKh 4.9.7: May they carry away all evil-doing. We invoke Agni with our songs.
Agni has shone with bright radiance; Sūrya has shone loftily in the sky; Sūrya has shone in heaven.

Offered with oblations of clarified butter, like the radiant Sūrya, place the offerings in Agni; in Agni place the sacred prayers (*brahmāṇi*) exclusively. O Agni, [place] the great [offering] at the sacrifice for the worshipper who follows thee with clarified butter.
Thus, O Agni, Vatsa has magnified thee with songs accompanied by strength.
Vena, the knower of the world, perceived that wherein all things have a single nest. This cow, being born, milked out this [world]; the hosts sang toward the one who finds the light.
Let the Gandharva, knowing it, proclaim that immortal name which is hidden in the cave.

RvKh 4.10.2b: Three steps of his are placed in secret; he who knows them shall be the father of the Father. RvKh 4.10.3a: He is the kinsman, the progenitor, and the ordainer; he knows all the abodes and all the worlds. RvKh 4.10.3b: There, in the third station, the gods, having attained immortality, exerted themselves.
Vena beheld that supreme station where all becomes one. This cow, being born, milked out this [world] for those who find the light; the Virāj uttered it aloud.
Let the Gandharva, though knowing it not, proclaim separately the immortal [truth], that supreme abode which is hidden in the cave.

Three steps have you taken into the secret places; he who knows them is the father of the father. He is our kinsman, our progenitor, and our ordainer; he knows all abodes and all worlds, where the gods, having attained immortality, took firm stand in a common dwelling.

He has encompassed all beings; the first-born of Cosmic Order proclaims this. As a speaker among speakers, he stands firm in the worlds; Agni, the impetuous one, has established his seat for the sake of leading us forward.
Having traversed heaven and earth in an instant, he has extended the thread of Cosmic Order for all to behold.
The god, guarding his own divinity, distinguishes between two who share a common kinship. Who is he?
That immortal [principle] by which all this—past, present, and future—is encompassed;

that by which the sacrifice with its seven priests is extended: may my mind be auspicious in its resolve. That by which the skillful and wise performers of action accomplish their rites at the sacrifices and in the assemblies.
RvKh 4.11.2b: That unprecedented spirit which dwells within living beings—may that mind of mine be auspicious in its resolve.
RvKh 4.11.3a: That which is wisdom, as well as consciousness and fortitude, that light which is immortal among living beings;
RvKh 4.11.4a: That divine [light] which rises far away from the waking man, even so does it go for the sleeping man.
May that mind of mine, which travels far, the one light among lights, be auspicious in its intentions.
In which the Ṛg-verses, the Sāman-chants, and the Yajus-formulas are established, like the spokes in the hub of a chariot wheel;
in which all consciousness is woven—may that mind of mine be auspicious in its intentions.
Like a skilled charioteer who guides horses with reins, he leads men like spirited steeds.
When the sixty-third body of the sacrifice here— which has nine naves and is primordial— is offered...
May that mind of mine, which consists of ten, five, thirty, and what is beyond—that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
Those [bricks] which are five, fifteen, a hundred, a thousand, a myriad, and a hundred million—those bricks of the sacrificial altar, that body; may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

I know this great Puruṣa, resplendent as the sun, beyond the darkness. May my mind be auspicious in its resolve, [so that] the wise may [perceive] me. May it be so. May my mind be auspicious in its resolve.

That by which the wise and the inspired priests perform their rites through speech, mind, and action— that consciousness toward which all living beings move— may that mind of mine be auspicious in its intentions. Those gods who are the mind and the heart, and those who move manifoldly in the intermediate space...
May that mind of mine be of auspicious intent, by which the ear and the two eyes move;
by which the fierce heaven, the earth, the intermediate space, the mountains, the intermediate directions, and the cardinal directions [are sustained];
and by which this world is pervaded, knowing it as it is—may that mind of mine be of auspicious intent.
That by which all this world came into being, and those gods who arose from the Great One, O Jātavedas— may that single light of Agni, born of austerity, be my mind, intent upon auspicious resolve.
This [is] for you.
May those cows whose udder has four openings, filled with honey and ghee—
may they be many, rich in milk, and dripping with ghee in our stall. May they come near, bestowing refreshing bliss, nourishment, and vital strength.
Yielding inexhaustible milk, enter my lineage so that I may become preeminent.
O Nejameṣa, fly away; as a good son, fly back again.
Bestow a male embryo upon this woman of mine who desires a son.
Just as this earth, being broad and wide, has received the embryo,
so do you place that embryo within her for birth in the tenth month—
with the preeminent form of Viṣṇu, in this noble woman, in the womb.
Bestow upon us a male child so that he may be born in the tenth month. We invoke Agni, who possesses a brilliant countenance, with our songs for his protection; may he carry us across our enemies.
