*Oṃ*. *Saṃjñānam*: [The seer is] Pañcakāśyapa; *Saṃjñāna* is the name. *Śamyur-uttamā*: that is a prayer (*āśīḥ*), a *śakvarī* metre, and it applies everywhere. *Nairhastyam*: this triplet is for the removal of the handless one, slaying rivals, and shattering armies; it is in the *ānuṣṭubha* metre, with a *bṛhatī* in the middle. *Pra*: [The seers are] Saptakaśyapa, Jamadagni, and Śamyu; the first is addressed to Agni (*āgneyī*), a *gāyatrī* metre; the second is a prayer (*āśīḥ*); the third is a praise of syllables (*akṣara-stuti*), which is an *anuṣṭubh*; the fourth is addressed to Soma (*saumī*); the fifth is addressed to Sūrya (*saurī*). *Vidā*: there are ten feet and five [verses]. Viśvāmitra [is the seer]; Indra or Prajāpati [is the deity]; it is addressed to Indra (*aindram*), purifying (*pāvanam*), in the *ānuṣṭubha* metre. The *purīṣa-padas* are addressed to Agni and Viṣṇu (*āgneya-vaiṣṇava*). *Ain*... [end of fragment].

The [verses] for Dru, Pūṣan, and the Devas are Vairāja; the second and fifth are Uṣṇih; the fourth is Nyaṅkusāriṇī; the seventh is Purastād-bṛhatī; the ninth and the last two are Paṅkti. "Agni" consists of eleven [syllables]; these are Yajus formulas whose deities are indicated by their wording.

The *vāyu* [section] consists of seven verses; the *praugam* has its deities stated; it is in the *gāyatrī* meter; the sixth verse is a *śakvarī*; there are five *yājuṣa* [verses]. [The section beginning with] "hotā" consists of twelve verses; either Vasiṣṭha [is the seer]; the *praiṣa-sūktas* [beginning with] the first *āpri* have their deities indicated by their characteristic marks (*liṅga-ukta-devata*); another [section] is called "unexpressed" (*anirukta*) because its deities are mentioned in its own sacrifice; [the section beginning with] "ajaid" consists of eleven verses; the seventh and ninth are *triṣṭubh*s. [The section beginning with] "devam hotā" consists of eighteen verses; "hotā" [consists of] twelve verses; this triplet [beginning with] "idam" was composed by Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva; the *Kuntāpa* [section] consists of two *bṛhatī*s and an *anuṣṭubh*. [The section beginning with] "vacyasvaḥ" is in the *ānuṣṭubh* meter up to the end; the four verses [beginning with] "rājñaḥ" [end with a *paṅkti*]; "indraḥ" ends with a *paṅkti*; "yaḥ" consists of five verses; "yaṣ" consists of six.

These five [verses] minus two belong to Etaśa; the sage [is Aitaśa]; there are sixty [syllables]; the eighth and ninth are *uṣṇih* meters; the last is a *dvipadā*; or they are *yajus* formulas—four of them.

"Vitatau" (is) six *ānuṣṭubh* verses. "Ihettha" is a group of four *dvipadā*s. "Bhuk" is a one-footed *nicṛt*. "Vi" and "Ime" are *anuṣṭubh*s. "Ādityāḥ" consists of five *jagatī*s, a *triṣṭubh*, an *upariṣṭād-bṛhatī*, a *purastād-bṛhatī*, a *dvipadā*, or a *yajus*. "Tvam" is a triplet (*ṛc*) of *ānuṣṭubh* meter. "Yad" is the dialogue between the *daśahotṛ* and the *pratigartṛ*; "nākapṛtsu" is a *jagatī*; the first [verse] is a *jagatī*, and the first [of the next set] is a *jagatī*.
Uśanas has spoken for recognition; Varuṇa has spoken for recognition.
Indra and Agni have spoken for mutual understanding; Savitṛ has spoken for recognition. May there be recognition between us and our own people, and recognition with those who are strangers.
May the Aśvins bestow concord upon us here;
may they establish it among us. That bond of union which Kakṣīvat, the son of the Aṅgirases, discovered—by means of that, O All-Gods, may you today make us all in harmony.
May our minds be in harmony; may we be of one intention and one purpose.
That person who is of discordant mind, him we bring into agreement.
We choose that auspiciousness for ourselves: a path for the sacrifice, a path for the lord of the sacrifice. May there be divine well-being for us, and well-being for human beings.
RvKh 5.2.1a: This oblation, which causes the army to flee like a wheel-track, [is called] *nairhastya*.
RvKh 5.2.1b: With that oblation, we wither the arms of our enemies. RvKh 5.2.2a: Indra and Pūṣan have turned their paths away.
Of those of yours who have been consumed by fire and hidden by fire, let Indra slay them one by one, each in turn.
Let there be no place for them among these [people], just as there is no room for the thought of a deer.
Let him seek out the enemies far away; let the cow come hither.
O Lord of the sacrifices, O Vasu, O Hotṛ of excellent wisdom!
For you the Gāyatra is chanted.
Kaśyapa, desiring cattle, desiring food, and desiring offspring—[has offered this].
The past and the future chant forth the Great Brahman, the one syllable; the manifold Brahman, the one syllable.
That syllable which the creators of beings and all the gods worship, they made the great seer Jamadagni its protector.

By the portion of King Soma, by the sacred word, may the quarters and intermediate directions be auspicious for us, who are endowed with heroic power. That brilliance of yours which was seen as pure light, hidden in the highest secret—that the seer Kaśyapa praises: the true Brahman, moving and unmoving; the firm Brahman, moving and unmoving.
The triple life-span of Jamadagni, the triple life-span of Kaśyapa;
the triple life-span of Agastya, that which is the triple life-span of the gods—may that triple life-span be ours.
We choose that well-being for ourselves: a path for the sacrifice, a path for the lord of the sacrifice; may there be divine prosperity for us, and prosperity for human beings.
RvKh 5.3.7b: May the medicine rise upward; may it be well-being for our bipeds and well-being for our quadrupeds.
RvKh 5.4.1a: O Maghavan, find [the way]; find the path; declare the directions according to the sacred word. RvKh 5.4.2a: With these aids, O wise one, make us mindful through your wisdom.
O Indra, [come] for glory, for food, for indeed Śakra is thus [our helper].
O wielder of the thunderbolt, most powerful wielder of the thunderbolt, you strive for wealth and for strength;
O most bountiful wielder of the thunderbolt, you strive [for us]. Come hither, drink, and rejoice!
RvKh 5.4.4a: Find for us wealth and heroic strength; become the lord of spoils according to our desire.
RvKh 5.4.4b: O most munificent wielder of the thunderbolt, you who are the mightiest among heroes, you strive for our success.
RvKh 5.4.5a: You who are the most generous among the liberal patrons, O wise one, lead us forward.
Indra knows him; I praise him, for the powerful Śakra is the subduer.
We invoke him for protection, the unconquered victor.
May he carry us across our enemies—he who is wisdom, desire, and the great cosmic order (ṛta).

We invoke Indra for the winning of wealth, the unconquered conqueror. May he carry us across our enemies; may he carry us across those who obstruct us. O Lord of the Stone, O Bounteous One, bestow upon us that ancient favor of yours.
O most powerful one, fulfillment belongs eternally to you, for the mighty Śakra rules over all.
O Lord, slayer of Vṛtra, you surely consider him a new man among the people.
Let us two speak together concerning others—of that hero who goes forth for the sake of cattle, the very kind friend who is free from duplicity. //5//
Thus indeed, thus indeed, O Agni;
thus indeed, thus indeed, O Viṣṇu;
thus indeed, thus indeed, O Indra.
For thus indeed, O Pūṣan;
for thus indeed, O gods;
for thus indeed is Śakra, for Śakra is the controller according to his will.
Agni kindled by the gods;
Agni kindled by Manu;
Agni well-kindled.
The Hotṛ chosen by the gods; the Hotṛ chosen by Manu;
the leader of sacrifices.
The charioteer of the sacrifices;
the invincible Hotṛ;
the swift bearer of oblations.
May the god carry the gods;
may the god Agni sacrifice to the gods;
may he, Jātavedas, perform the rites. //7//
May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink of the Soma;
he who is praised by the Maruts, whose host is the Maruts,
who has the Maruts as his friends, and who is strengthened by the Maruts.
Slaying Vṛtra, he released the waters together with the might of the Maruts;
the gods rejoiced after him when he did so.
In the crossing of the waters, in the overcoming of Vṛtra, in the slaying of Śambara, and in the quest for cattle—
[he praises you] who sings with secret steps.
In this most distant realm,
the Brahmanas increase him with invincible power through their might.
Performing service for the gods,
together with the Maruts as his friends—
may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, hear us here; may he drink of the Soma here.
May the god Premān protect the invocation of the gods with divine wisdom. May this sacred formulation (brahman) prosper; may this ruling power (kṣatra) prosper.
May he protect this one who presses the juice, the sacrificer;
may the Wondrous One [come] with his wondrous aids.
May he hear our sacred prayers and approach us with his protection. //8//
May the divine Indra drink the Soma;
he who is the most heroic among those born once,
and the strongest among those born many times.
The rider of the bay horses;
the offspring of Pṛśni;
the wielder of the thunderbolt.
The breaker of forts, the shatterer of forts,
the releaser of the waters.
Leader of the waters,
leader of the warriors,
slayer of enemies, far-renowned.
The doer of wonders, possessed of wondrous deeds,
the willing god has come here;
may Indra, the god, hear us here and drink the soma here.
May the god protect these [people] at the invocation of the gods with divine thought; may he protect this spiritual power (*brahman*); may he protect this ruling power (*kṣatra*).
May he protect this pressing sacrificer with his wondrous aids;
may the divine Savitṛ, the golden-handed one with the beautiful tongue, drink of the Soma.
Subāhu with beautiful fingers;
three times a day performing the true libation;
when he brought forth both treasuries of wealth, the two who delight in the impulse to give.
They pressed out the most excellent [juice] dedicated to Savitṛ:
a milch-cow that yields milk, and a draft-ox that carries the load.
The swift steed;
the victorious one standing upon the chariot;
the wise woman, the Purandhi.
May he drive away disease from this assembly of young men; may he drive away the malevolent.
May the god Savitṛ hear us here; may he rejoice here in the soma.
May the god favor this invocation of the gods with divine thought; may he favor this spiritual power (*brahman*), may he favor this ruling power (*kṣatra*).
May he protect this one who presses the juice, the sacrificer,
with his wondrous aids.
May Heaven and Earth be exhilarated by the Soma.
The father and the mother;
the son and the offspring;
the cow and the bull.
And Dhanyā and Dhiṣaṇā; Suretā and Sudugdhā; Śambhū and Mayobhū.
The vigorous and the full of milk;
the bestower of seed and the consumer of seed;
may Heaven and Earth hear us here, and may they rejoice here in the Soma.
May these two goddesses favor this invocation of the gods with divine wisdom; may they favor this spiritual power (brahman), may they favor this ruling power (kṣatra).
May the R̥bhus protect this sacrificing one who presses the Soma, with their wondrous aids, O wondrous ones. May the divine R̥bhus exhilarate themselves with the Soma.
Having performed their work with skillful hands, they are active in their tasks;
they are wealthy and most prosperous.
By skill you are most skilled;
by power you are most powerful—
those who protected the all-inspiring, omniform cow.
Protecting [the world], he became the cow possessing all forms; he yoked the two bay steeds and approached the gods with his life-force.
The young ones woke up together, rejoicing; after a year, the skillful workers came to their share in the sacrifice.
The Rbhus, as gods, have heard us here; here let them exhilarate themselves with Soma.
May the gods favor this invocation of the gods with divine thought; may they favor this sacred power (*brahman*), may they favor this ruling power (*kṣatra*).
May all the gods protect this pressing sacrificer with their various aids; may they be exhilarated by the soma.
All are Vaiśvānara; all are of universal majesty;
they have magnified the Great One.
Swift as the wind, they are led by the path of the earth; they carry the cooked offerings, closely united; their breath is the wind, and they are impelled by fire.
Those who have taken their stand upon heaven and earth, upon the waters and the sky, and upon the *brahman* and the *kṣatra*.
The sacrificial grass and the altar;
the sacrifice and the wide mid-air;
you who are the three times eleven.
And thirty-three;
and three hundred and three;
and three thousand and three.
So many are the Abhiṣācas; so many are the Rātiṣācas;
so many are the wives.
So many are the women;
so many are in the place of departure; so many are in the place of rest.
O gods, do not leave us behind; do not exclude us from your favor. O all-gods, hear this here; here let yourselves be exhilarated by Soma.
O gods, favor this invocation of the gods with divine thought.
May this spiritual power (brahman) prevail; may this ruling power (kṣatra) prevail;
may they protect this sacrificer who presses the soma.
Variegated with manifold aids,
may Agni Vaiśvānara, the kindler of all the gods, be exhilarated by Soma.
The eternal divine light,
which shines for the human tribes,
gleaming through the ancient days.
In the face of the ageless dawns,
he who shines upon the sky and upon the earth,
across the wide mid-air.
May he grant protection for the sacrifice with his light.
May Agni Vaiśvānara hear us here; may he rejoice here in the Soma.
May the god favor this invocation of ours with divine wisdom.
May this Brahman prevail; may this Kṣatra prevail;
may it protect this Soma-pressing sacrificer.
Variegated with their variegated aids,
the Maruts, the gods, have become exhilarated by the Soma; they are well-praising and good singers.
The Arka-stubhas, of great vigor, heroes with unassailable chariots,
brilliant ones whose mother is Pṛśni.
The bright ones with golden jaws, the powerful ones who grant blessings, those who possess the splendor of the clouds and are clothed in radiant colors.
May the Maruts, the gods, hear us here; may they exhilarate themselves here with Soma. May these gods favor this invocation of the gods with divine wisdom. May this sacred prayer be successful!
May this kṣatra prevail;
may they protect this pressing sacrificer with their various aids.
May Agni Jātavedas, the fair-faced one with wondrous radiance, the never-absent master of the house who is visible even through the darkness, be exhilarated by the Soma.
Worthy of praise with offerings of clarified butter,
he whose path is broad and strewn with sacrifices;
the unconquered victor who overcomes his enemies through his counter-attack.
O Agni Jātavedas, bestow upon us splendor and conquering power; grant it in abundance, even in profusion! Protect the one who kindles you and the praiser from distress.
May Agni Jātavedas hear us here; may he exhilarate himself here with the Soma.
May the god favor this invocation of the gods with divine insight.
May this sacred formulation (brahman) prevail; may this sovereign power (kṣatra) prevail;
may it protect this sacrificer who presses the soma.
Variegated with his variegated aids—
O singer, in the exhilaration of this soma, may Indra be intoxicated; O singer, in the exhilaration of this, may Indra slay the serpent Ahi.
In the exhilaration of this [Soma], O singer, Indra slew Vṛtra;
in the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra set in motion the rush of the waters;
in the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra quickened the swift and swelled the unconquered.
In his exhilaration, O singer, Indra raised up the Aryan race; he overcame the Dāsas and established the people.
In his exhilaration, O singer, Indra propped up the sky, spread out the earth, and extended the mid-air.
In his exhilaration, O singer, Indra stilled the agitated oceans;
in his exhilaration, O singer, Indra stilled the agitated mountains that were crashing like bellowing *ṛśya* deer.
In his exhilaration, O singer, may Indra hear us here and may he delight here in the soma.
May the god, with divine thought, favor this invocation of the gods; may he favor this spiritual power (brahman), may he favor this ruling power (kṣatra).
May he protect this pressing sacrificer with his wondrous aids;
may Vāyu, the first-goer and lover of sacrifice, come to the sacrifice together with the mind.
Auspicious with his auspicious teams of horses;
O heroes, gods, and lords whose paths are golden, come for our aid—
Vāyu and Indra, the bounteous patrons.

O two kings of poetic wisdom, come with your mental power to the dwelling of the skillful one; O destroyers of enemies, come to the place of assembly. O two divine *adhvaryu* priests, come on your chariot with a sun-bright skin.
With honey you two anoint the sacrifice.
Indra is most worthy of praise with hymns, the lord of spoils and the master of riches;
he, the possessor of bay horses, is the friend of those who have pressed the soma.
We invoke all the gods, well-adorned, at this sacrifice.
May those gods come to this sacrifice with divine thought,
taking pleasure in the rite— those who are the makers of the body of the sacrifice and who sit at the sacrificial session.
O Viśvā, for the drinking of Soma!
At this sacrifice, [I invoke] the great goddess Vāc, the well-adorned Vāc, with my speech.
(Praiṣa-adhyāya)
Let the Hotṛ worship Agni, who is well-kindled with excellent fuel upon the navel of the earth, at the gathering of wealth.
Let him partake of the ghee at the summit of heaven, in the place of the sacrificial food; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
Let the Hotṛ worship Tanūnapāt, the offspring of Aditi, the guardian of the world.
May the god today anoint for the gods the paths leading to the gods with honey; may he partake of the clarified butter—O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
The Hotṛ shall worship Narāśaṃsa, the one praised by men, the leader of men.
May he be rich in fatness through cattle, powerful through heroes, foremost in chariots, and radiant with gold; may he partake of the clarified butter—O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
Let the Hotṛ worship Agni; praised with the *iḍā*-invocation, may the god bring the gods hither—the unerring messenger, the bearer of oblations.
May he favor this sacrifice, may the god favor this invocation of the gods; let him partake of the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
Let the Hotṛ worship the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), well-spread and soft as wool. In this sacrifice, may it spread wide and far, providing a comfortable seat for the gods.
May the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas sit upon this dear [seat] today; may Indra accept the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to the lofty, cavern-dwelling doors that carry the vessels; let them open with their frames, and let them be supported by the wide-spreading [posts].
Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Dawn and Night, the two great ones, beautiful to look upon, who prepare a dwelling for men as wives for their husbands.
While Indra and the gods are smiling, let them sit upon this sacred grass (*barhis*); let them partake of the clarified butter (*ājya*). O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
Let the Hotṛ worship the two divine Hotṛs, the two pleasant Potṛs, the two sages, the two wise ones.

May one of them today perform the well-sacrificed rite with nourishment (*iṣ*), and may the other, through his own power, perform it with strength (*ūrj*) and a favorable disposition. May they place this sacrifice among the gods in heaven; let them partake of the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to the three goddesses, the most skillful in their work; may they today extend this flawless labor.
Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Tvaṣṭṛ, the most brilliant, the skillful, the bestower of seed, the possessor of all wealth, and the bestower of glory.
Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Vanaspati; may the men, seeking his favor, offer him worship as he delights in our prayers.
May the axe, self-sharpened, according to the seasons, today carry the oblation from the god to the gods; may it partake of the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
Let the Hotṛ worship Agni, the well-born, with the clarified butter—Svāhā! To the fat—Svāhā! To the drops—Svāhā! To the consecrated offerings—Svāhā! To the hymns of the oblation—Svāhā!
Agni has conquered; he has won the prize. The god, the carrier of oblations, has brought [the offering] down for the gods.
Being urged by the forward-flowing streams of milk and being made ready, prolonging the life of the sacrifice—O Hotṛ, give the command for the oblations to the gods!
Let the Hotṛ worship Agni; may he enjoy the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Soma; may he enjoy the oblation of clarified butter; O Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Agni and Soma; may they enjoy the fat of the omentum of the goat; O Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Agni and Soma; may they enjoy the sacrificial cake; O Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Agni and Soma; let them eat today of the goat-offering, the fat extracted from the middle, before the onslaught of the gods and before the human seizure. Truly, they shall now enjoy the portions taken from the flanks, the haunches, the tail, and from every limb of these [animals] that are first in the pasture of the fields, well-flowing with milk, belonging to the hundred Rudras, consumed by Agni, and clothed in fat. Let Agni and Soma indeed perform this; let them relish the oblation. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
O Lord of the Forest, golden-leaved, bring the offerings for the gods; your purpose has been known from of old.
Having fastened him with a girth-rope that moves to the right, lead him along the straightest paths of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*).
Let the Hotṛ worship Vanaspati, for he has been bound with a most finely ground and most powerful girth-rope.

Where are the beloved abodes of Agni’s oblation of clarified butter; where are the beloved abodes of Soma’s oblation of clarified butter; where are the beloved abodes of the goat-oblation of Agni and Soma; where are the beloved paths of Vanaspati; where are the beloved abodes of the gods who drink the clarified butter; where are the beloved abodes of Agni the Hotṛ—there, having praised him and extolled him, may he cast this [oblation] down, making it most effective as if by joining it together; thus may the divine Vanaspati enjoy the oblation; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
O Lord of the Forest, having bound [the victim] with a cord made of the finest flour, you who know the sacred ways, carry the oblations to the gods; and do you proclaim the giver among the immortals.

Let the Hotṛ worship Agni Sviṣṭakṛt. Agni has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Agni’s oblation of clarified butter; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Soma’s oblation of clarified butter; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of the oblation of the goat for Agni and Soma; he has sacrificed to the dear paths of Vanaspati; let him sacrifice to the dear abodes of the gods who drink clarified butter; let him sacrifice to the dear abodes of Agni the Hotṛ; let him sacrifice to his own greatness. May the sacrifice offer nourishment; may Jātavedas, the knower of beings, enjoy the oblations at this rite. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

This sacrificer has chosen you, Agni, as the Hotṛ today—cooking the cooked offerings, cooking the sacrificial cake, taking the clarified butter for Agni, taking the clarified butter for Soma, and binding the goat for Agni and Soma. Today the divine Tree has become well-established; with the clarified butter for Agni, with the clarified butter for Soma, and with the goat for Agni and Soma, they have offered it. Cook that fat portion thoroughly; they have grasped it and they have increased it with the sacrificial cake. O Ṛṣi, descendant of Ṛṣis, grandson of Ṛṣis, this sacrificer has chosen you today from among many who have assembled.

RvKh 5.7.3a: May the divine *barhis* be well-disposed toward the gods; may it be rich in heroes through the heroes. At dawn it should be spread, at night it should be gathered. May we rejoice, surpassing others in wealth, as masters of the *barhis*. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, let it come. Sacrifice! RvKh 5.7.3b: O divine doors, firm in their closing, yielding in their path, yet fixed and steadfast at the invocation of the gods—may a young calf measure them out, or a newborn boy. Let not a dusty, crumbling wall fall upon them. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, let them open wide. Sacrifice!

The two goddesses, Dawn and Night, have invoked one another at this sacrifice as it proceeds; even now, may the divine hosts have arrived. Well-pleased and well-disposed, may they partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of winning wealth. Sacrifice!

The two goddesses, the Loving Ones, the repositories of wealth—of whom one drives away evil hatreds, while the other brings desirable riches to the sacrificer. May they partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of winning wealth. Sacrifice!

RvKh 5.7.3e: O two divine offerings of strength (*ūrja-āhutī*), let one bring food and strength; let the other bring the shared meal and the drinking together. May we, sharing with the living, be protected by the former, and by the former, the latter. Those two offerings of strength, bestowing strength, have bestowed that strength upon us. Let them partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of gaining wealth. Sacrifice! RvKh 5.7.3f:

O divine gods, the two divine Hotṛ-priests, Potṛ-priests, and Neṣṭṛ-priests, who have struck down the evil speaker and brought forth wealth—let them partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of gaining wealth. Sacrifice!

The three goddesses, the three goddesses—Iḍā, Sarasvatī, and Bhāratī—Bhāratī has touched the sky with the Ādityas; Sarasvatī has protected this sacrifice here with the Rudras. May we rejoice right here in the shared banquet with the wealthy Iḍā. For the winning of wealth and the granting of treasure, may they partake; perform the sacrifice!

RvKh 5.7.3h: The divine Narāśaṃsa has three heads and six eyes; a hundred white-backed ones support him, and a thousand carry him forward. O Mitra and Varuṇa, this is his office as Hotṛ; O Bṛhaspati, his praise; O Aśvins, his office as Adhvaryu. For the winning of wealth, let there be the offering of the treasury of wealth—sacrifice! RvKh 5.7.3i: The divine Vanaspati, clothed in rain and dripping with ghee, has touched the sky with his summit, filled the mid-air with his middle, and made firm the earth with his base. For the winning of wealth, let there be the offering of the treasury of wealth—sacrifice!

RvKh 5.7.3k: Divine is the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) of the waters, the unshakable foundation of all that is subject to falling away; it is the granter of desires, much desired, glorious. Through this sacrificial grass, may we overcome all other grasses. For the winning of wealth, let there be a share of the treasure-bestowing gift. Sacrifice! RvKh 5.7.3l: May the divine Agni Sviṣṭakṛt—the possessor of beautiful wealth, the delightful sage, whose thoughts are true, the sacrificing priest—perform the sacrifice for the Hotṛ after every Hotṛ who has sacrificed. O Agni, those gods whom you have sacrificed to, those whom you have sent forth, they have rejoiced in your office as Hotṛ.

Send this sacrifice, which has attained its goal and goes to the gods, to the gods in heaven. And you, O Agni, being the Sviṣṭakṛt, have become the Hotṛ; for the winning of wealth, at the utterance of "namas," enjoy the offering and perform the sacrifice for the bestowal of wealth.

Let the Hotṛ worship Indra, the lord of the bay horses; may Indra, accompanied by Pūṣan, eat the parched grains; accompanied by Sarasvatī and the Bhāratī, may he eat the groats; the rice-offering belongs to Indra, the milk-curd to Mitra and Varuṇa. May Indra, graciously accepting the oblation set forth for the morning pressing, partake of it; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Indra, the lord of bay horses; may Indra, accompanied by Pūṣan, eat the parched grains; may he, accompanied by Sarasvatī and the Bhāratī, eat the groats; the scattered grain belongs to Indra, and the cake belongs to the midday pressing—may Indra, enjoying the offerings set forth, come;

O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Indra, the lord of bay horses; may Indra, accompanied by Pūṣan, eat the parched grains; may he, accompanied by Sarasvatī and the Bhāratī, eat the groats; the scattered grain belongs to Indra, and the cake belongs to the third pressing—may Indra, enjoying the offering set forth, come; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Indra and Vāyu, who are worthy and licking [the offering]. Let them be brought forward, rich in cattle with their cattle-seeking [teams]. Of these two, let the hero’s bright teams, led by cattle, come forward. O Hero, let the whip be before the horses; let there be their departure here, O believer, and let him effect their unyoking. May Indra and Vāyu enjoy it, partake, and drink the Soma. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Mitra and Varuṇa, the noble rulers, the destroyers of enemies, who watch over us with unblinking and observant eyes; they are the best finders of the path even for the blind. Contemplating the eternal Law (ṛta) with their flawless vision, may Mitra and Varuṇa act accordingly; may they accept it, enjoy it, and drink the Soma. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the Aśvins, the Nāsatyas, whose fires shine brightly, who travel on the paths of Rudra. Between your two wheels, bring hither for us desirable food and strength. May the two, with their well-bred heroes, drive away the bloodless enemies by the path that leads across. O youthful ones, bedewed with honey, sprinkle this sacrifice; may the Aśvins accept it, enjoy it, and drink the Soma—O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Indra. May he come from afar, from nearby, from the wide mid-air, or from his own dwelling place; for him, these bright Soma juices, dripping with sweetness, have been poured forth for Indra. May he take pleasure in them; may he come and drink the Soma. Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Indra—the eater, the drinker, the hearer of the call, the one who comes to this prayer, the fulfiller of the wish of the pressing sacrificer, and the increaser [of his strength]—who partakes of the exclusive portion of the midday libation. Let him fill both his flanks with the slaying of Vṛtra and the slaying of Māhīnā. These pure and stirred Soma juices have been set forth for Indra; may he take pleasure in them, may he come and drink the Soma. Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Indra for the third libation, accompanied by the Ṛbhus, the Vibhus, the Vājas, Bṛhaspati, and all the gods. May his exhilarations of the morning be united, may those of midday be united, and may those of the evening be united. Of these [Soma juices] that have been sprinkled together, like a wild ox plunging forward, do thou, O Bull, with thy two arms, come hither with thy two bay steeds. Flushing thy jaws, spreading them wide, O thou who drinkest the dregs! These strong, pressed Soma juices, mixed with milk, have been set forth for Indra; may he take pleasure in them, may he approach, may he drink the Soma. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
Let the Hotṛ worship Indra accompanied by the Maruts; may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, enjoy it, let it come, let him drink the Soma—O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

He has spoken this for this pressing sacrificer; let them perform it. Thus let the Ādityas enjoy it, let them rejoice, let them partake, let them drink, let them delight in the Soma—O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the god Savitṛ. May he drive away disease; may he drive away the one who speaks evil. He has granted a good instigation; may he grant that for this pressing sacrificer. Thus may the god Savitṛ be pleased; may he be exhilarated; may he come and drink the Soma. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Today this sacrificer, pressing the Soma and cooking the cooked offerings, has chosen Agni as the Hotṛ; he is preparing the sacrificial cakes, taking up the clarified butter for Agni, taking up the clarified butter for Soma, binding the goat for Agni, pressing the Soma for Indra, and parching the grains for the two bay horses. Today the divine Vanaspati has become well-disposed toward Agni with the clarified butter, toward Soma with the clarified butter, toward Agni with the goat, toward Indra with the Soma, and toward the two bay horses with the parched grains. You two have eaten.

From the fat, he has cooked; he has grasped it; he has strengthened himself with the sacrificial cakes. Indra has drunk the Soma mixed with milk, mixed with barley, and of intense flavor. With its thick middle, he has risen up; the exhilarations have expanded his heart. He has drunk the Vimada draught and has grown strong through our hymns of praise. O Seer, descendant of Seers, grandson of Seers, you whom the sacrificing patron who presses the juice has chosen today from among many who have assembled.

O Indra, drink from the *dhānā-soma* (barley-grain and soma); for your two bay horses have been held fast. Let them smell the *dhānā*s and the dregs (*ṛjīṣa*). O you who move with your chariot, pour out [the soma], for if they should ask you, "Where did you rejoice with these wives?"—[answer]: "With this pressing sacrificer. What have you bestowed upon him? Excellent heroic power, the climax of the sacrifice's impulse. Whatever he has desired, that has come to pass exactly so. Hotṛ, sacrifice!

O Maghavan Indra, here indeed is your exhilaration; tomorrow there shall be a Soma-pressing for you accompanied by the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, the Ṛbhus, the Vibhus, the Vājins, Bṛhaspati, and all the gods. O Brahman, announce it to Agni and Indra, to Mitra and Varuṇa, to the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, and to all the gods who are priests, partakers of Soma, and drinkers of Soma. O Brahman, restrain your speech!

Let the Hotar sacrifice to the Aśvins for the Soma-pressings of the day after tomorrow; let them come on their circuit three times, and let them honor us three times a day. And furthermore, O Nāsatyas, O Gods, grant a fourth portion for the sake of the prize-winner! May Agni, whose horses are ruddy and who drips with ghee, be in harmony [with us];
may Uṣas, with her ruddy steeds, be in harmony [with us].

Accompanied by the Sun and the Etaśas, let the Hotṛ worship Indra from the office of the Hotṛ; together with Heaven and Earth and according to the season, let him drink the Soma. O Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice!
Let the Hotṛ worship the Maruts from the office of the Potṛ—those who are well-praising and fair-singing; together with the season, let them drink the Soma. O Potṛ, perform the sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Tvaṣṭṛ, the well-born, from the office of the Neṣṭṛ; may he drink Soma with the wives of the gods and according to the season. O Neṣṭṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Agni from the office of the Āgnīdhra; may he drink Soma with the season. O Āgnīdh, sacrifice!
Let the Hotṛ worship Indra, the Brahman, from the office of the Brahman; may he drink Soma with the season. O Brahman, sacrifice!

RvKh 5.7.5g: Let the Hotṛ worship the god Draviṇodas; let him drink Soma from the Hotṛ’s cup with the seasonal offerings. O Hotṛ, sacrifice! RvKh 5.7.5h: Let the Hotṛ worship the god Draviṇodas; let him drink Soma from the Potṛ’s cup with the seasonal offerings. O Potṛ, sacrifice! RvKh 5.7.5i: Let the Hotṛ worship the god Draviṇodas; let him drink Soma from the Neṣṭṛ’s cup with the seasonal offerings. O Neṣṭṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the god Draviṇodas. He has drunk from the Hotṛ’s cup, he has drunk from the Potṛ’s cup, he has drunk from the Neṣṭṛ’s cup; let the fourth cup, uninjured, immortal, the drink of Indra, the god Draviṇodas, drink of the offerings of Draviṇodas.
Having himself extended [the sacrifice], having himself encouraged it—with this self-encouraged invocation—let him drink of the Soma with the seasonal rites. O Acchāvāka, perform the sacrifice!

RvKh 5.7.5l: Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to the Aśvins as Adhvaryus; let them drink the Soma from the Adhvaryu’s portion according to the season; let the two Adhvaryus perform the sacrifice. RvKh 5.7.5m: Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Agni Gṛhapati from the Gārhapatya fire. O Agni, you are a good householder; may the sacrificer who presses [the Soma] be a good householder. May you, through this pressing sacrificer, be a good householder; may you, through this pressing sacrificer, be a good householder.
